<h1 id="pagerduty-api">PagerDuty API v2.0.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

This document describes the PagerDuty REST APIs.

For guides and examples please visit our [Documentation.](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/get-started/getting-started/)

Our REST APIs are defined in OpenAPI v3.x. You can view the schema at [github.com/PagerDuty/api-schema](https://github.com/PagerDuty/api-schema).

Note that properties in some schemas have fields not shown by default such as `readOnly`, `format`, and `default`. Hover your cursor over the right column that looks like `optional+1` to see the full list of fields.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://api.pagerduty.com">https://api.pagerduty.com</a> - PagerDuty V2 API.

Email: <a href="mailto:support@pagerduty.com">PagerDuty Support</a> 
Web: <a href="http://www.pagerduty.com/support">PagerDuty Support</a> 

# Authentication

* API Key (api_key)
    - Parameter Name: **Authorization**, in: header. The API Key with format `Token token=<API_KEY>`

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-abilities">Abilities</h1>

This describes your account's abilities by feature name. For example `"teams"`.
An ability may be available to your account based on things like your pricing plan or account state.


## List abilities

<a id="opIdlistAbilities"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/abilities \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /abilities`

List all of your account's abilities, by name.

"Abilities" describes your account's capabilities by feature name. For example `"teams"`.

An ability may be available to your account based on things like your pricing plan or account state.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#abilities)

Scoped OAuth requires: `abilities.read`


<h3 id="list-abilities-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "abilities": [
    "teams",
    "read_only_users",
    "service_support_hours",
    "urgencies"
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Not Found",
    "code": 2100
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Not Found",
    "code": 2100
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Not Found",
    "code": 2100
  }
}
```

<h3 id="list-abilities-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|An array of ability names.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Caller did not supply credentials or did not provide the correct credentials.<br>If you are using an API key, it may be invalid or your Authorization header may be malformed.<br>|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Caller is not authorized to view the requested resource.<br>While your authentication is valid, the authenticated user or token does not have permission to perform this action.<br>|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests have been made, the rate limit has been reached.|Inline|

<h3 id="list-abilities-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|abilities|[string]|true|none|The set of abilities your account has.|

## Test an ability

<a id="opIdgetAbility"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/abilities/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /abilities/{id}`

Test whether your account has a given ability.

"Abilities" describes your account's capabilities by feature name. For example `"teams"`.

An ability may be available to your account based on things like your pricing plan or account state.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#abilities)

Scoped OAuth requires: `abilities.read`

|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-add-ons">Add-ons</h1>

Developers can write their own functionality to insert into PagerDuty's UI.


## List installed Add-ons

<a id="opIdlistAddon"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/addons \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /addons`

List all of the Add-ons installed on your account.

Addon's are pieces of functionality that developers can write to insert new functionality into PagerDuty's UI.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#add-ons)

Scoped OAuth requires: `addons.read`


<h3 id="list-installed-add-ons-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results per page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Offset to start pagination search results.|
|total|query|boolean|false|By default the `total` field in pagination responses is set to `null` to provide the fastest possible response times. Set `total` to `true` for this field to be populated.<br><br>See our [Pagination Docs](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for more information.<br>|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|include[]|query|string|false|Array of additional Models to include in response.|
|service_ids[]|query|[string]|false|Filters the results, showing only Add-ons for the given services|
|filter|query|string|false|Filters the results, showing only Add-ons of the given type|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|
|include[]|services|
|filter|full_page_addon|
|filter|incident_show_addon|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "addons": [
    {
      "id": "PKX7619",
      "type": "full_page_addon_reference",
      "summary": "Internal Status Page",
      "self": "https://api.pagerduty.com/addons/PKX7619",
      "html_url": null,
      "name": "Internal Status Page",
      "src": "https://intranet.example.com/status"
    }
  ],
  "limit": 25,
  "offset": 0,
  "more": false,
  "total": null
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Not Found",
    "code": 2100
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Not Found",
    "code": 2100
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Not Found",
    "code": 2100
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Not Found",
    "code": 2100
  }
}
```

<h3 id="list-installed-add-ons-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A paginated array of installed Add-ons.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Caller provided invalid arguments. Please review the response for error details. Retrying with the same arguments will *not* work.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Caller did not supply credentials or did not provide the correct credentials.<br>If you are using an API key, it may be invalid or your Authorization header may be malformed.<br>|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Caller is not authorized to view the requested resource.<br>While your authentication is valid, the authenticated user or token does not have permission to perform this action.<br>|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests have been made, the rate limit has been reached.|Inline|

## Install an Add-on

<a id="opIdcreateAddon"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/addons \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "addon": {
      "type": "full_page_addon",
      "name": "Internal Status Page",
      "src": "https://intranet.example.com/status"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /addons`

Install an Add-on for your account.

Addon's are pieces of functionality that developers can write to insert new functionality into PagerDuty's UI.

Given a configuration containing a `src` parameter, that URL will be embedded in an `iframe` on a page that's available to users from a drop-down menu.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#add-ons)

Scoped OAuth requires: `addons.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "addon": {
    "type": "full_page_addon",
    "name": "Internal Status Page",
    "src": "https://intranet.example.com/status"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="install-an-add-on-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|The Add-on to be installed.|
|» addon|body|[Addon](#schemaaddon)|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "addon": {
    "id": "PKX7619",
    "type": "full_page_addon_reference",
    "summary": "Internal Status Page",
    "self": "https://api.pagerduty.com/addons/PKX7619",
    "html_url": null,
    "name": "Internal Status Page",
    "src": "https://intranet.example.com/status"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Not Found",
    "code": 2100
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Not Found",
    "code": 2100
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Not Found",
    "code": 2100
  }
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Not Found",
    "code": 2100
  }
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The Add-on that was installed.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Caller provided invalid arguments. Please review the response for error details. Retrying with the same arguments will *not* work.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Caller did not supply credentials or did not provide the correct credentials.<br>If you are using an API key, it may be invalid or your Authorization header may be malformed.<br>|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Caller is not authorized to view the requested resource.<br>While your authentication is valid, the authenticated user or token does not have permission to perform this action.<br>|Inline|

## Update an Add-on

<a id="opIdupdateAddon"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/addons/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "addon": {
      "type": "full_page_addon",
      "name": "Internal Status Page",
      "src": "https://intranet.example.com/status"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /addons/{id}`

Update an existing Add-on.

Addon's are pieces of functionality that developers can write to insert new functionality into PagerDuty's UI.

Given a configuration containing a `src` parameter, that URL will be embedded in an `iframe` on a page that's available to users from a drop-down menu.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#add-ons)

Scoped OAuth requires: `addons.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "addon": {
    "type": "full_page_addon",
    "name": "Internal Status Page",
    "src": "https://intranet.example.com/status"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-add-on-parameters">Parameters</h3>

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-alert-grouping-settings">Alert Grouping Settings</h1>

Alert Grouping Settings allow you to configure how alerts in services are grouped together into incidents.


## List alert grouping settings

<a id="opIdlistAlertGroupingSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/alert_grouping_settings \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /alert_grouping_settings`

List all of your alert grouping settings including both single service settings and global content based settings.

The settings part of Alert Grouper service allows us to create Alert Grouping Settings and configs that are required to be used during grouping of the alerts.

Scoped OAuth requires: `services.read`

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/alert_grouping_settings \

        ]
      },
      "services": [
        {
          "id": "P0KJZ0A"
        },
        {
          "id": "PA15YRT"
        }
      ]

```

`POST /alert_grouping_settings`

Create a new Alert Grouping Setting.

The settings part of Alert Grouper service allows us to create Alert Grouping Settings and configs that are required to be used during grouping of the alerts.

This endpoint will be used to create an instance of AlertGroupingSettings for either one service or many services that are in the alert group setting.

Scoped OAuth requires: `services.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "alert_grouping_setting": {
    "id": "PZC4OM1",
    "name": "Example of Alert Grouping Setting",
    "description": "This Alert Grouping Setting is an example",
    "type": "content_based",
    "config": {
      "time_window": 900,
      "aggregate": "all",
      "fields": [

      }
    ]
  }
}
```

`DELETE /alert_grouping_settings/{id}`

## Get aggregated incident data

<a id="opIdgetAnalyticsMetricsIncidentsAll"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/analytics/metrics/incidents/all \

  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "filters": {
      "created_at_start": "2024-01-01T00:00:00-05:00",
      "created_at_end": "2024-01-31T00:00:00-05:00",
      "urgency": "high",
      "major": true,
      "team_ids": [
        "PGVXG6U",
        "PNVU4U4"
      ],
      "service_ids": [
        "PQVUB8D",
        "PU2D9X3"
      ]
    },
    "aggregate_unit": "day",
    "time_zone": "Etc/UTC"
  }'
```

`POST /analytics/metrics/incidents/all`

Provides aggregated enriched metrics for incidents.

The provided metrics are aggregated by day, week, month using the aggregate_unit parameter, or for the entire period if no aggregate_unit is provided.

<!-- theme: info -->
> A `team_ids` or `service_ids` filter is required for [user-level API keys](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/using-the-api#section-generating-a-personal-rest-api-key) or keys generated through an OAuth flow. Account-level API keys do not have this requirement.
<!-- theme: info -->
> **Note:** Data availability reflects [pipeline processing cycles](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/insights#:~:text=Data%20Update%20Schedule) and is generally within 24 hours under normal conditions.

Scoped OAuth requires: `analytics.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filters": {
    "created_at_start": "2024-01-01T00:00:00-05:00",
    "created_at_end": "2024-01-31T00:00:00-05:00",
    "urgency": "high",
    "major": true,
    "team_ids": [
      "PGVXG6U",
      "PNVU4U4"
    ],
    "service_ids": [
      "PQVUB8D",
      "PU2D9X3"
    ]
  },
  "aggregate_unit": "day",
  "time_zone": "Etc/UTC"
}
```

<h3 id="get-aggregated-incident-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|body|body|[AnalyticsModel](#schemaanalyticsmodel)|false|Parameters and filters to apply to the dataset.|
|» filters|body|object|false|Accepts a set of filters to apply to the Incidents before aggregating.  Any incidents that do not match the included filters will be omitted from the results.|
|» » created_at_start|body|string|false|Accepts an ISO8601 DateTime string. Any incidents with a created_at less than this value will be omitted from the results. The maximum supported time range in conjunction with created_at_end is one year.|
|» » created_at_end|body|string|false|Accepts an ISO8601 DateTime string. Any incidents with a created_at greater than or equal to this value will be omitted from the results. The maximum supported time range in conjunction with created_at_start is one year.|
|» » urgency|body|string|false|Any incidents whose urgency does not match the provided string will be omitted from the results.|
|» » major|body|boolean|false|A boolean flag including whether results should contain *only* [major incidents](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/operational-reviews#major-incidents), or exclude major incidents. If no value is provided all incidents will be included.|
|» » min_ackowledgements|body|integer|false|An integer that sets the requirement for the minimum number of acknowledgements to occur on an incident. For example, setting this to 1 will return only incidents that have at least 1 acknowledgement. If no value is provided, all incidents will be included.|
|» » min_timeout_escalations|body|integer|false|An integer that sets the requirement for the minimum number of timeout escalations to occur on an incident. For example, setting this to 1 will return only incidents that have at least 1 timeout escalation. If no value is provided, all incidents will be included.|
|» » min_manual_escalations|body|integer|false|An integer that sets the requirement for the minimum number of manual escalations to occur on an incident. For example, setting this to 1 will return only incidents that have at least 1 manual escalation. If no value is provided, all incidents will be included.|
|» » team_ids|body|[string]|false|An array of team IDs. Only incidents related to these teams will be included in the results. If omitted, all teams the requestor has access to will be included in the results.|
|» » service_ids|body|[string]|false|An array of service IDs. Only incidents related to these services will be included in the results. If omitted, all services the requestor has access to will be included in the results.|
|» » escalation_policy_ids|body|[string]|false|An array of escalation policy IDs. Only incidents related to these escalation policies will be included in the results. If omitted, all escalation policies the requestor has access to will be included in the results.|
|» » priority_ids|body|[string]|false|An array of priority IDs. Only incidents with these priorities will be included in the results. If omitted, all priorities will be included in the results.|
|» » priority_names|body|[string]|false|An array of user-defined priority names. Only incidents with these priorities will be included in the results. If omitted, all priorities will be included in the results.|
|» » pd_advance_used|body|boolean|false|If true, only incidents where PD Advance was used will be included in the results, and vice versa. If omitted, all incidents will be included.|
|» time_zone|body|string|false|The time zone to use for the results and grouping. Must be in tzdata format. See list of accepted values [here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones).|
|» order|body|string|false|The order in which the results were sorted; asc for ascending, desc for descending.|
|» order_by|body|string|false|The column that was used for ordering the results.|
|» aggregate_unit|body|string \| null|false|The time unit to aggregate metrics by.  If no value is provided, the metrics will be aggregated for the entire period.|

## Get aggregated escalation policy data

<a id="opIdgetAnalyticsMetricsIncidentsEscalationPolicy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/analytics/metrics/incidents/escalation_policies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "filters": {
      "created_at_start": "2023-06-10T00:00:00-07:00",
      "created_at_end": "2023-06-11T23:59:59-07:00",
      "urgency": "high",
      "major": true,
      "escalation_policy_ids": [
        "PDESCP1",
        "PDESCP2"
      ]
    },
    "time_zone": "Etc/UTC"
  }'
```

`POST /analytics/metrics/incidents/escalation_policies`

Provides aggregated metrics for incidents aggregated into units of time by escalation policy.

Example metrics include Seconds to Resolve, Seconds to Engage, Snoozed Seconds, and Sleep Hour Interruptions. Metric definitions can be found in our [Knowledge Base](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/insights#escalation-policy-list).

<!-- theme: info -->
> **Note:** Data availability reflects [pipeline processing cycles](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/insights#:~:text=Data%20Update%20Schedule) and is generally within 24 hours under normal conditions.

Scoped OAuth requires: `analytics.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filters": {
    "created_at_start": "2023-06-10T00:00:00-07:00",
    "created_at_end": "2023-06-11T23:59:59-07:00",
    "urgency": "high",
    "major": true,
    "escalation_policy_ids": [
      "PDESCP1",
      "PDESCP2"
    ]
  },
  "time_zone": "Etc/UTC"
```

## Get aggregated metrics for all escalation policies

<a id="opIdgetAnalyticsMetricsIncidentsEscalationPolicyAll"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/analytics/metrics/incidents/escalation_policies/all \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```

`POST /analytics/metrics/incidents/escalation_policies/all`

Provides aggregated metrics across all escalation policies.

Example metrics include Seconds to Resolve, Seconds to Engage, Snoozed Seconds, and Sleep Hour Interruptions. Metric definitions can be found in our [Knowledge Base](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/insights#escalation-policy-list).

<!-- theme: info -->
> **Note:** Data availability reflects [pipeline processing cycles](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/insights#:~:text=Data%20Update%20Schedule) and is generally within 24 hours under normal conditions.

## Get aggregated service data

<a id="opIdgetAnalyticsMetricsIncidentsService"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/analytics/metrics/incidents/services \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "filters": {
      "created_at_start": "2023-06-10T00:00:00-07:00",
      "created_at_end": "2023-06-11T23:59:59-07:00",
      "urgency": "high",
      "major": true,
      "team_ids": [
        "P3XUQ75"
      ],
      "service_ids": [
        "PPSCXAN"
      ]
    },
    "aggregate_unit": "day",
    "time_zone": "Etc/UTC"
  }'
```

`POST /analytics/metrics/incidents/services`

Provides aggregated metrics for incidents aggregated into units of time by service.

Example metrics include Seconds to Resolve, Seconds to Engage, Snoozed Seconds, and Sleep Hour Interruptions. Metric definitions can be found in our [Knowledge Base](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/insights#services-list).
Data can be aggregated by day, week or month in addition to by service, or provided just as a collection of aggregates for each service in the dataset for the entire period.  If a unit is provided, each row in the returned dataset will include a 'range_start' timestamp.

<!-- theme: info -->
> **Note:** Data availability reflects [pipeline processing cycles](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/insights#:~:text=Data%20Update%20Schedule) and is generally within 24 hours under normal conditions.

Scoped OAuth requires: `analytics.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filters": {
```

## Get aggregated metrics for all services

<a id="opIdgetAnalyticsMetricsIncidentsServiceAll"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/analytics/metrics/incidents/services/all \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "filters": {
      "created_at_start": "2023-06-17T00:00:00-07:00",
      "created_at_end": "2023-07-01T23:59:59-07:00",
      "service_ids": [
        "PQVUB8D",
        "PU2D9X3"
      ]
    },
    "time_zone": "Etc/UTC"
  }'
```

`POST /analytics/metrics/incidents/services/all`

Provides aggregated metrics across all services.

Example metrics include Seconds to Resolve, Seconds to Engage, Snoozed Seconds, and Sleep Hour Interruptions. Metric definitions can be found in our [Knowledge Base](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/insights#services-list).

<!-- theme: info -->
> A `team_ids` or `service_ids` filter is required for [user-level API keys](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/using-the-api#section-generating-a-personal-rest-api-key) or keys generated through an OAuth flow. Account-level API keys do not have this requirement.
<!-- theme: info -->
> **Note:** Data availability reflects [pipeline processing cycles](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/insights#:~:text=Data%20Update%20Schedule) and is generally within 24 hours under normal conditions.

Scoped OAuth requires: `analytics.write`

## Get aggregated team data

<a id="opIdgetAnalyticsMetricsIncidentsTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/analytics/metrics/incidents/teams \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "filters": {
      "created_at_start": "2023-06-10T00:00:00-07:00",
      "created_at_end": "2023-06-11T23:59:59-07:00",
      "urgency": "high",
      "major": true,
      "team_ids": [
        "P3XUQ75"
      ]
    },
    "aggregate_unit": "day",
    "time_zone": "Etc/UTC"
  }'
```

`POST /analytics/metrics/incidents/teams`

Provides aggregated metrics for incidents aggregated into units of time by team.

Example metrics include Seconds to Resolve, Seconds to Engage, Snoozed Seconds, and Sleep Hour Interruptions. Metric definitions can be found in our [Knowledge Base](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/insights#teams-list).
Data can be aggregated by day, week or month in addition to by team, or provided just as a collection of aggregates for each team in the dataset for the entire period.  If a unit is provided, each row in the returned dataset will include a 'range_start' timestamp.

<!-- theme: info -->
> A `team_ids` or `service_ids` filter is required for [user-level API keys](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/using-the-api#section-generating-a-personal-rest-api-key) or keys generated through an OAuth flow. Account-level API keys do not have this requirement.
<!-- theme: info -->
> **Note:** Data availability reflects [pipeline processing cycles](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/insights#:~:text=Data%20Update%20Schedule) and is generally within 24 hours under normal conditions.

Scoped OAuth requires: `analytics.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filters": {
    "created_at_start": "2023-06-10T00:00:00-07:00",
    "created_at_end": "2023-06-11T23:59:59-07:00",
    "urgency": "high",
    "major": true,
    "team_ids": [
      "P3XUQ75"
    ]
  },
  "aggregate_unit": "day",
  "time_zone": "Etc/UTC"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|» » created_at_end|body|string|false|Accepts an ISO8601 DateTime string. Any incidents with a created_at greater than or equal to this value will be omitted from the results. The maximum supported time range in conjunction with created_at_start is one year.|
|» » urgency|body|string|false|Any incidents whose urgency does not match the provided string will be omitted from the results.|
|» » major|body|boolean|false|A boolean flag including whether results should contain *only* [major incidents](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/operational-reviews#major-incidents), or exclude major incidents. If no value is provided all incidents will be included.|
|» » min_ackowledgements|body|integer|false|An integer that sets the requirement for the minimum number of acknowledgements to occur on an incident. For example, setting this to 1 will return only incidents that have at least 1 acknowledgement. If no value is provided, all incidents will be included.|
|» » min_timeout_escalations|body|integer|false|An integer that sets the requirement for the minimum number of timeout escalations to occur on an incident. For example, setting this to 1 will return only incidents that have at least 1 timeout escalation. If no value is provided, all incidents will be included.|

For example, setting this to 1 will return only incidents that have at least 1 manual escalation. If no value is provided, all incidents will be included.|

|» » priority_names|body|[string]|false|An array of user-defined priority names. Only incidents with these priorities will be included in the results. If omitted, all priorities will be included in the results.|
|» » pd_advance_used|body|boolean|false|If true, only incidents where PD Advance was used will be included in the results, and vice versa. If omitted, all incidents will be included.|

|» aggregate_unit|body|string \| null|false|The time unit to aggregate metrics by.  If no value is provided, the metrics will be aggregated for the entire period.|

## Get aggregated PD Advance usage data

<a id="opIdgetAnalyticsMetricsPdAdvanceUsageFeatures"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/analytics/metrics/pd_advance_usage/features \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
```

## Get aggregated metrics for all responders

<a id="opIdgetAnalyticsMetricsRespondersAll"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/analytics/metrics/responders/all \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "filters": {
      "date_range_start": "2023-06-10T00:00:00-07:00",

        "PDUSER1",
        "PDUSER2"
      ]

    "time_zone": "Etc/UTC"
  }'
```

`POST /analytics/metrics/responders/all`

Provides aggregated incident metrics for all selected responders.

Example metrics include Seconds to Resolve, Seconds to Engage, Snoozed Seconds, and Sleep Hour Interruptions. Metric definitions can be found in our [Knowledge Base](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/insights#responders-list).

<!-- theme: info -->
> **Note:** Data availability reflects [pipeline processing cycles](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/insights#:~:text=Data%20Update%20Schedule) and is generally within 24 hours under normal conditions.

Scoped OAuth requires: `analytics.write`

```json
  "filters": {
    "date_range_start": "2023-06-10T00:00:00-07:00",

    "urgency": "high",
    "responder_ids": [
      "PDUSER1",
      "PDUSER2"
    ]
  },
  "time_zone": "Etc/UTC"
}
```

## Get aggregated metrics for all users

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/analytics/metrics/users/all \
  -X POST \

  }'
```

`POST /analytics/metrics/users/all`

Provides aggregated metrics across all users within their account. This endpoint provides summary statistics about user activity and performance.

<!-- theme: info -->
> **Note:** Data availability reflects [pipeline processing cycles](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/insights#:~:text=Data%20Update%20Schedule) and is generally within 24 hours under normal conditions.

Scoped OAuth requires: `analytics.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filters": {
    "created_at_start": "2024-08-07T00:00:00-07:00",
    "created_at_end": "2025-08-05T23:59:59-07:00"
  },
  "time_zone": "America/Chicago"
}
```

`POST /analytics/raw/incidents`

Provides enriched incident data and metrics for multiple incidents.

Example metrics include Seconds to Resolve, Seconds to Engage, Snoozed Seconds, and Sleep Hour Interruptions. Metric definitions can be found in our [Knowledge Base](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/insights#incidents-list).

<!-- theme: info -->
> A `team_ids` or `service_ids` filter is required for [user-level API keys](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/using-the-api#section-generating-a-personal-rest-api-key) or keys generated through an OAuth flow. Account-level API keys do not have this requirement.
<!-- theme: info -->
> **Note:** Data availability reflects [pipeline processing cycles](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/insights#:~:text=Data%20Update%20Schedule) and is generally within 24 hours under normal conditions.

Scoped OAuth requires: `analytics.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filters": {
    "created_at_start": "2024-01-01T00:00:00-05:00",
    "created_at_end": "2024-01-31T00:00:00-05:00",
    "updated_after": "2024-05-01T00:00:00-05:00",
    "urgency": "high",
    "major": true,
    "team_ids": [
      "PGVXG6U",
      "PNVU4U4"
    ],
    "service_ids": [
      "PQVUB8D",
      "PU2D9X3"
    ],
    "priority_names": [
      "P1",
      "P2"
    ],
    "incident_type_ids": [
      "PIJ90N7",
      "PKL73Z2"
    ]
  },
  "limit": 20,
  "order": "desc",
  "order_by": "created_at",
  "time_zone": "Etc/UTC"
}
```

<h3 id="get-raw-data---multiple-incidents-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|Parameters and filters to apply to the dataset.|
|» filters|body|object|false|Filters the result, only show incidents that match the conditions passed in the filter.|
|» » created_at_start|body|string|false|Filters the result, showing only the incidents where the creation timestamp is greater than or equal to the filter value.|
|» » created_at_end|body|string|false|Filters the result, showing only the incidents where the creation timestamp is less than the filter value.|
|» » updated_after|body|string|false|Filters the result, showing only incidents where the updated_at value is greater than the filter value.|
|» » urgency|body|string|false|Filters the result, showing only the incidents where urgency matches the filter value.|
|» » major|body|boolean|false|An incident is classified as a [major incident](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/operational-reviews#major-incidents) if it has one of the two highest priorities, or if multiple responders are added and acknowledge the incident.|
|» » team_ids|body|[string]|false|An array of team IDs. Only incidents that are assigned to a member of these teams will be returned. Account must have the teams ability to use this parameter.|
|» » service_ids|body|[string]|false|An array of service IDs. Only results related to these services will be returned.|
|» » priority_ids|body|[string]|false|The priority_ids filter applied to the results.|
|» » priority_names|body|[string]|false|The priority_names filter applied to the results.|
|» » incident_type_ids|body|[string]|false|Filter incidents by specific incident type IDs. Only incidents matching the given IDs will be returned.|
|» starting_after|body|string|false|A cursor to indicate the reference point that the results should follow|
|» ending_before|body|string|false|A cursor to indicate the reference point that the results should precede|
|» order|body|string|false|The order the results;  asc for ascending, desc for descending. Defaults to 'desc'.|
|» order_by|body|string|false|The column to use for ordering the results. Defaults to 'created_at'.|
|» limit|body|integer|false|Number of results to include in each batch.<br>Limits between 1 to 1000 are accepted.|
|» time_zone|body|string|false|The time zone to use for the results.|

`GET /analytics/raw/incidents/{id}/responses`

Provides enriched responder data for a single incident.

Example metrics include Time to Respond, Responder Type, and Response Status. See metric definitions below.

```json
  "order": "desc",

}
```

`POST /analytics/raw/responders/{responder_id}/incidents`

Provides enriched incident data and metrics for a specific responder.

Example metrics include Mean Seconds to Resolve, Mean Seconds to Engage, Snoozed Seconds, and Sleep Hour Interruptions. Metric definitions can be found in our [Knowledge Base](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/insights#incidents-list).

<!-- theme: info -->
> **Note:** Data availability reflects [pipeline processing cycles](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/insights#:~:text=Data%20Update%20Schedule) and is generally within 24 hours under normal conditions.

Scoped OAuth requires: `analytics.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filters": {
    "created_at_start": "2023-06-10T00:00:00-07:00",
    "created_at_end": "2023-06-11T23:59:59-07:00",
    "incident_type_ids": [
      "PIJ90N7",
      "PKL73Z2"
    ]
  },
  "responder_id": "PDUSER1",
  "limit": 100,
  "order": "asc",
  "order_by": "incident_created_at",
  "time_zone": "Etc/UTC"
}
```

<h3 id="get-raw-incidents-for-a-single-responderid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|responder_id|path|string|true|The ID of the responder.|
|body|body|object|false|Parameters and filters to apply to the dataset.|
|» filters|body|object|false|Filters the result, only show incidents that match the conditions passed in the filter.|
|» » created_at_start|body|string|false|Filters the result, showing only the incidents where the creation timestamp is greater than the filter value.|
|» » created_at_end|body|string|false|Filters the result, showing only the incidents where the creation timestamp is less than the filter value.|
|» » urgency|body|string|false|Filters the result, showing only the incidents where urgency matches the filter value.|
|» » major|body|boolean|false|An incident is classified as a [major incident](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/operational-reviews#major-incidents) if it has one of the two highest priorities, or if multiple responders are added and acknowledge the incident.|
|» » team_ids|body|[string]|false|An array of team IDs. Only incidents that are assigned to a member of these teams will be returned. Account must have the teams ability to use this parameter.|
|» » service_ids|body|[string]|false|An array of service IDs. Only results related to these services will be returned.|
|» » priority_ids|body|[string]|false|The priority_ids filter applied to the results.|
|» » priority_names|body|[string]|false|The priority_names filter applied to the results.|
|» » incident_type_ids|body|[string]|false|Filter incidents by specific incident type IDs. Only incidents matching the given IDs will be returned.|
|» starting_after|body|string|false|A cursor to indicate the reference point that the results should follow|
|» ending_before|body|string|false|A cursor to indicate the reference point that the results should precede|
|» order|body|string|false|The order in which to display the results; asc for ascending, desc for descending. Defaults to `desc`.|
|» order_by|body|string|false|The column to use for ordering the results. Defaults to `incident_created_at`.|
|» limit|body|integer|false|Number of results to include in each batch.<br>Limits between 1 to 1000 are accepted.|
|» time_zone|body|string|false|The time zone to use for the results.|

`POST /analytics/raw/users`

Allows users to retrieve a raw list of user analytics data within their account. This endpoint provides detailed data about user activity and account configuration.

<!-- theme: info -->
> **Note:** Data availability reflects [pipeline processing cycles](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/insights#:~:text=Data%20Update%20Schedule) and is generally within 24 hours under normal conditions.

Scoped OAuth requires: `analytics.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "filters": {
    "created_at_start": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "created_at_end": "2025-09-01T00:00:00Z"
  },
  "limit": 10
}
```

|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|

|» filters|body|[AnalyticsUserFilterConditions](#schemaanalyticsuserfilterconditions)|false|none|
|» time_zone|body|string|false|The time zone to use for the results and grouping. Must be in tzdata format. See list of accepted values [here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones).|
|» order|body|string|false|The order in which the results were sorted; asc for ascending, desc for descending.|
|» order_by|body|string|false|The column that was used for ordering the results.|
|» aggregate_unit|body|string \| null|false|The time unit to aggregate metrics by. If no value is provided, the metrics will be aggregated for the entire period.|
|» limit|body|integer|false|The maximum number of results to return per page. The default (and maximum allowed value) is 1000.|
|» starting_after|body|string \| null|false|A cursor used for pagination. Starting after cursor provides the next set of results in forward pagination order.|

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-audit">Audit</h1>

Provides audit record data.


## List audit records

<a id="opIdlistAuditRecords"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/audit/records \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /audit/records`

List audit trail records matching provided query params or default criteria.

The returned records are sorted by the `execution_time` from newest to oldest.

See [`Cursor-based pagination`](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for instructions on how to paginate through the result set.

Only admins, account owners, or global API tokens on PagerDuty account [pricing plans](https://www.pagerduty.com/pricing) with the "Audit Trail" feature can access this endpoint.

For other role based access to audit records by resource ID, see the resource's API documentation.

For more information see the [Audit API Document](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/audit-records-api/).

Scoped OAuth requires: `audit_records.read`


<h3 id="list-audit-records-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|The minimum of the `limit` parameter used in the request or the maximum request size of the API.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Optional parameter used to request the "next" set of results from an API.  The value provided here is most commonly obtained from the `next_cursor` field of the previous request.  When no value is provided, the request starts at the beginning of the result set.<br>|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the date range over which you want to search. If not specified, defaults to `now() - 24 hours` (past 24 hours)|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the date range over which you want to search. If not specified, defaults to `now()`. May not be more than 31 days after `since`.|
|root_resource_types[]|query|string|false|Resource type filter for the root_resource.|
|actor_type|query|string|false|Actor type filter.|
|actor_id|query|string|false|Actor Id filter. Must be qualified by providing the `actor_type` param.|
|method_type|query|string|false|Method type filter.|
|method_truncated_token|query|string|false|Method truncated_token filter. Must be qualified by providing the `method_type` param.|

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-automation-actions">Automation Actions</h1>

Automation Actions invoke jobs that are staged in Runbook Automation or Process Automation.


## List Automation Actions

<a id="opIdgetAllAutomationActions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/automation_actions/actions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /automation_actions/actions`

Lists Automation Actions matching provided query params.

The returned records are sorted by action name in alphabetical order.

See [`Cursor-based pagination`](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for instructions on how to paginate through the result set.


<h3 id="list-automation-actions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|The minimum of the `limit` parameter used in the request or the maximum request size of the API.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Optional parameter used to request the "next" set of results from an API.  The value provided here is most commonly obtained from the `next_cursor` field of the previous request.  When no value is provided, the request starts at the beginning of the result set.<br>|
|name|query|string|false|Filters results to include the ones matching the name (case insensitive substring matching)|
|runner_id|query|string|false|Filters results to include the ones linked to the specified runner.<br>Specifying the value `any` filters results to include the ones linked to runners only,<br>thus omitting the results not linked to runners.<br>|
|classification|query|[AutomationActionsActionClassificationEnum](#schemaautomationactionsactionclassificationenum)|false|Filters results to include the ones matching the specified classification (aka category)|
|team_id|query|string|false|Filters results to include the ones associated with the specified team.|
|service_id|query|string|false|Filters results to include the ones associated with the specified service|
|action_type|query|string|false|Filters results to include the ones matching the specified action type|

|classification|remediation|

## Create an Automation Action

<a id="opIdcreateAutomationAction"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/automation_actions/actions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "action": {
      "name": "Restart apache",
      "description": "Restarts apache on the us-west-2-shopping-cart host",
      "action_type": "script",
      "action_data_reference": {
        "script": "java --version"
      },
      "teams": [
        {
          "id": "PQ9K7I8",
          "type": "team_reference"
        }
      ],
      "services": [
        {
          "id": "PRDRWUJ",
          "type": "service_reference"
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

## Update an Automation Action

<a id="opIdupdateAutomationAction"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/automation_actions/actions/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "action": {
      "name": "Restart apache",
      "description": "Restarts apache on the us-west-2-shopping-cart host",
      "action_classification": "diagnostic",
      "action_type": "process_automation",
      "runner": "string",
      "only_invocable_on_unresolved_incidents": false,
      "allow_invocation_manually": true,
      "allow_invocation_from_event_orchestration": true,
      "map_to_all_services": false,
      "action_data_reference": {
        "script": "print(\"Hello from a Python script!\")",
        "invocation_command": "/usr/local/bin/python3"
      }
    }
  }'
```

## List Automation Action runners

<a id="opIdgetAutomationActionsRunners"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/automation_actions/runners \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /automation_actions/runners`

Lists Automation Action runners matching provided query params.
The returned records are sorted by runner name in alphabetical order.

See [`Cursor-based pagination`](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for instructions on how to paginate through the result set.


<h3 id="list-automation-action-runners-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|The minimum of the `limit` parameter used in the request or the maximum request size of the API.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Optional parameter used to request the "next" set of results from an API.  The value provided here is most commonly obtained from the `next_cursor` field of the previous request.  When no value is provided, the request starts at the beginning of the result set.<br>|
|name|query|string|false|Filters results to include the ones matching the name (case insensitive substring matching)|
|include[]|query|[string]|false|Includes additional data elements into the response|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|
|include[]|associated_actions|

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-paused-incident-reports">Paused Incident Reports</h1>

Provides paused Incident reporting data on services and accounts that have paused Alerts.


## Get Paused Incident Reporting on Alerts

<a id="opIdgetPausedIncidentReportAlerts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/paused_incident_reports/alerts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /paused_incident_reports/alerts`

Returns the 5 most recent alerts that were triggered after being paused and the 5 most recent alerts that were resolved after being paused for a given reporting period (maximum 6 months lookback period).  Note: This feature is currently available as part of the Event Intelligence package or Digital Operations plan only.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#paused-incident-reports)

Scoped OAuth requires: `incidents.read`

|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the date range over which you want to search.|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the date range over which you want to search.|
|service_id|query|string|false|Specifies a filter to limit the scope of reporting to a particular service|
|suspended_by|query|string|false|Specifies a filter to scope the response to either alerts suspended by Auto Pause or Event Rules.|

## List the supporting Business Services for the given Business Service Id, sorted by impacted status.

<a id="opIdgetBusinessServiceSupportingServiceImpacts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/business_services/string/supporting_services/impacts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /business_services/{id}/supporting_services/impacts`

Retrieve of Business Services that support the given Business Service sorted by highest Impact with `status` included.
This endpoint does not return an exhaustive list of Business Services but rather provides access to the most impacted up to the limit of 200.

The returned Business Services are sorted first by Impact, secondarily by most recently impacted, and finally by name.

To get impact information about a specific set of Business Services, use the `ids[]` parameter on the `/business_services/impacts` endpoint.
Scoped OAuth requires: `services.read`


<h3 id="list-the-supporting-business-services-for-the-given-business-service-id-sorted-by-impacted-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|
|additional_fields[]|query|string|false|Provides access to additional fields such as highest priority per business service and total impacted count|
|ids[]|query|string|false|The IDs of the resources.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|additional_fields[]|services.highest_impacting_priority|
|additional_fields[]|total_impacted_count|

## Get the global priority threshold for a Business Service to be considered impacted by an Incident

<a id="opIdgetBusinessServicePriorityThresholds"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/business_services/priority_thresholds \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /business_services/priority_thresholds`

Retrieves the priority threshold information for an account.  Currently, there is a `global_threshold` that can be set for the account. <h1 id="pagerduty-api-change-events">Change Events</h1>

Change Events enable you to send informational events about recent changes such as code deploys and system config changes from any system that can make an outbound HTTP connection. These events do not create incidents and do not send notifications; they are shown in context with incidents on the same PagerDuty service.


## List Change Events

<a id="opIdlistChangeEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/change_events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /change_events`

List all of the existing Change Events.

Scoped OAuth requires: `change_events.read`


<h3 id="list-change-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results per page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Offset to start pagination search results.|
|total|query|boolean|false|By default the `total` field in pagination responses is set to `null` to provide the fastest possible response times. Set `total` to `true` for this field to be populated.<br><br>See our [Pagination Docs](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for more information.<br>|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|team_ids[]|query|[string]|false|An array of team IDs. Only results related to these teams will be returned. Account must have the `teams` ability to use this parameter.|
|integration_ids[]|query|[string]|false|An array of integration IDs. Only results related to these integrations will be returned.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the date range over which you want to search, as a UTC ISO 8601 datetime string. Will return an HTTP 400 for non-UTC datetimes.|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the date range over which you want to search, as a UTC ISO 8601 datetime string. Will return an HTTP 400 for non-UTC datetimes.|

## List related Change Events for an Incident

<a id="opIdlistIncidentRelatedChangeEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/string/related_change_events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /incidents/{id}/related_change_events`

List related Change Events for an Incident, as well as the reason these changes are correlated with the incident.

Change events represent service changes such as deploys, build completion, and configuration changes, providing information that is critical during incident triage or hypercare. For more information on change events, see [Change Events](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/change-events).

The Change Correlation feature provides incident responders with recent change events that are most relevant to that incident. Change Correlation informs the responder why a particular change event was surfaced and correlated to an incident based on three key factors which include time, related service, or intelligence (machine learning).

Scoped OAuth requires: `incidents.read`

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-enrichment-integrations">Enrichment Integrations</h1>

Enrichment Integrations synchronize external data sources into PagerDuty's Enrichment Service, producing enrichment schemas ("data tables") that you can use in Event Enrichment rules to add context to incoming events. The ServiceNow CMDB integration synchronizes Configuration Item (CI) data from your ServiceNow instance, mapping ServiceNow fields onto event fields.

<!-- theme: warning -->

> ### Early Access
> This API is in Early Access and may change at any time before General Availability. Contact your PagerDuty account team to request access.


## List ServiceNow integrations

<a id="opIdlistServiceNowIntegrations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/enrichment/integrations/servicenow \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /enrichment/integrations/servicenow`

Lists the ServiceNow enrichment integrations for the account, including their CMDB tables, field mappings, and credentials. Because only one integration is allowed per account, this returns at most one integration.

<!-- theme: warning -->

> ### Early Access
> This API is in Early Access and may change at any time. Contact your PagerDuty account team to request access.

Scoped OAuth requires: `contextual_data.read`


<h3 id="list-servicenow-integrations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "integrations": [
    {
      "id": "01HQXYZ9ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQR",
      "name": "Production CMDB Integration",
      "description": "Enrichment data from production ServiceNow instance",
      "cmdb_tables": [
        {
          "id": "01HTABC8DEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTU",
          "display_name": "Network Switches",
          "ci_table_name": "cmdb_ci_ip_switch",

          "field_mappings": [
            {
              "servicenow_field": "name",

              "type": "query"
            },
            {
              "servicenow_field": "support_group",
              "event_field": "Support Group",
              "type": "enriched"
```

## Create a ServiceNow integration

<a id="opIdcreateServiceNowIntegration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/enrichment/integrations/servicenow \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Production CMDB Integration",
    "description": "Enrichment data from production ServiceNow instance",
    "cmdb_tables": [
      {
        "display_name": "Network Switches",
        "ci_table_name": "cmdb_ci_ip_switch",
        "query_filter": "operational_status=1",
        "field_mappings": [
          {
            "servicenow_field": "name",
            "event_field": "source"
          },
          {
            "servicenow_field": "operational_status",
            "event_field": "Operational Status"
          },
          {
            "servicenow_field": "support_group",
            "event_field": "Support Group"
          },
          {
            "servicenow_field": "sys_class_name",
            "event_field": "CI Class"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /enrichment/integrations/servicenow`

Creates a ServiceNow enrichment integration with one or more CMDB table configurations. Only one integration is allowed per account. Each CMDB table must define between 2 and 20 field mappings, and an integration may contain at most 8 tables. Credentials are managed separately through the credentials endpoints.

<!-- theme: warning -->

> ### Early Access
> This API is in Early Access and may change at any time. Contact your PagerDuty account team to request access.

Scoped OAuth requires: `contextual_data.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Production CMDB Integration",
  "description": "Enrichment data from production ServiceNow instance",
  "cmdb_tables": [
    {
      "display_name": "Network Switches",
      "ci_table_name": "cmdb_ci_ip_switch",
      "query_filter": "operational_status=1",
      "field_mappings": [
        {
          "servicenow_field": "name",
          "event_field": "source"
        },
        {
          "servicenow_field": "operational_status",
          "event_field": "Operational Status"
        },
        {
          "servicenow_field": "support_group",
          "event_field": "Support Group"
        },
        {
          "servicenow_field": "sys_class_name",
          "event_field": "CI Class"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|The ServiceNow enrichment integration to create. Credentials are added separately through the credentials endpoint.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the integration.|
|» description|body|string|false|An optional description of the integration.|
|» cmdb_tables|body|[[ServiceNowTableInput](#schemaservicenowtableinput)]|true|The ServiceNow CMDB table configurations. An integration must have between 1 and 8 tables.|

## Update a CMDB table

<a id="opIdupdateServiceNowTable"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/enrichment/integrations/servicenow/string/tables/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "cmdb_table": {
      "display_name": "Production Network Switches",
      "ci_table_name": "cmdb_ci_ip_switch",
      "query_filter": "operational_status=1^u_environment=production",
      "field_mappings": [
        {
          "servicenow_field": "name",
          "event_field": "source"
        },
        {
          "servicenow_field": "operational_status",
          "event_field": "Operational Status"
        },
        {
          "servicenow_field": "sys_class_name",
          "event_field": "CI Class"
        },
        {
          "servicenow_field": "support_group.name",
          "event_field": "Support Team"
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /enrichment/integrations/servicenow/{integration_id}/tables/{table_id}`

Replaces a ServiceNow CMDB table configuration. This is a full replacement — all fields, including `ci_table_name` and the complete `field_mappings` list, must be provided. A table can only be updated while its synchronization is disabled and before its initial backfill has started.

<!-- theme: warning -->

> ### Early Access
> This API is in Early Access and may change at any time. Contact your PagerDuty account team to request access.

Scoped OAuth requires: `contextual_data.write`


> Body parameter

```json

  "cmdb_table": {
    "display_name": "Production Network Switches",
    "ci_table_name": "cmdb_ci_ip_switch",
    "query_filter": "operational_status=1^u_environment=production",
    "field_mappings": [
      {
        "servicenow_field": "name",
        "event_field": "source"
      },
      {
        "servicenow_field": "operational_status",
        "event_field": "Operational Status"
      },
      {
        "servicenow_field": "sys_class_name",
        "event_field": "CI Class"
      },
      {
        "servicenow_field": "support_group.name",
        "event_field": "Support Team"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|

|table_id|path|string|true|Base32-encoded UUID v7 (26 uppercase alphanumeric characters) identifying the CMDB table configuration.|
|body|body|object|true|The replacement CMDB table configuration. This is a full replacement — all fields, including `ci_table_name` and the complete `field_mappings` list, must be provided. A table can only be updated while its sync is disabled and before its initial backfill has started.|
|» cmdb_table|body|[ServiceNowTableInput](#schemaservicenowtableinput)|true|none|

## Enable CMDB table sync

<a id="opIdenableServiceNowTableSync"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/enrichment/integrations/servicenow/string/tables/string/enable \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /enrichment/integrations/servicenow/{integration_id}/tables/{table_id}/enable`

Enables data synchronization for a ServiceNow CMDB table configuration. Once enabled, the table's enrichment schema is populated with CI data from ServiceNow and kept up to date with periodic syncs. This operation is idempotent — enabling an already-enabled table succeeds.

<!-- theme: warning -->

> ### Early Access
> This API is in Early Access and may change at any time. Contact your PagerDuty account team to request access.

Scoped OAuth requires: `contextual_data.write`

|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|integration_id|path|string|true|Base32-encoded UUID v7 (26 uppercase alphanumeric characters) identifying the ServiceNow enrichment integration.|
|table_id|path|string|true|Base32-encoded UUID v7 (26 uppercase alphanumeric characters) identifying the CMDB table configuration.|

## Test a CMDB table

<a id="opIdtestServiceNowTable"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/enrichment/integrations/servicenow/string/tables/string/test \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /enrichment/integrations/servicenow/{integration_id}/tables/{table_id}/test`

Validates a ServiceNow CMDB table configuration by running a live query against ServiceNow and returning up to 10 sample records. Use this before enabling synchronization to confirm that the credentials, table name, query filter, and mapped fields are correct. Records are returned keyed by ServiceNow field name.

## Create ServiceNow credentials

<a id="opIdcreateServiceNowCredentials"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/enrichment/integrations/servicenow/credentials \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "credentials": {
      "instance_endpoint": "https://your-instance.service-now.com",
      "user": "integration_user",
      "password": "YOUR_SERVICENOW_PASSWORD"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /enrichment/integrations/servicenow/credentials`

Creates the ServiceNow API credentials used to authenticate synchronization and test requests. Only one credential set is allowed per account, and it is shared across the account's ServiceNow integration. The password is never returned in responses.

## Update ServiceNow credentials

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-enrichment-schemas">Enrichment Schemas</h1>

Enrichment Schemas are queryable "data tables" of contextual information that you can use in Event Enrichment to add context to incoming events. Each schema defines query fields (used to match events) and enriched fields (the data added to a match). CSV schemas can be created and populated directly, or generated automatically from an uploaded CSV file.

<!-- theme: warning -->

> ### Early Access
> This API is in Early Access and may change at any time before General Availability. Contact your PagerDuty account team to request access.


## Query enrichment data

<a id="opIdqueryEnrichmentData"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/enrichment/query \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "schema_id": "9f194d8d-0f58-4c5c-b1d2-a5adf7171821",
    "query": [
      {
        "field": "Application",
        "value": "Authorization"
      },
      {
        "field": "Environment",
        "value": "production"
      }
    ]
```

## Create an enrichment schema

<a id="opIdcreateEnrichmentSchema"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/enrichment/schemas \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "integration_type": "CSV",
    "name": "Application Environment Enrichment",
    "description": "Maps applications to team and runbook info by environment",
    "fields": [
      {
        "name": "Application",
        "type": "query"
      },
      {
        "name": "Environment",
        "type": "query"
      },
      {
        "name": "Manager",
        "type": "enriched"
      },
      {
        "name": "Team",
        "type": "enriched"
      },
      {
        "name": "Runbook URL",
        "type": "enriched"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /enrichment/schemas`

Creates an enrichment schema. Provide a JSON body to define the schema explicitly (returns `201`), or upload a CSV file as `multipart/form-data` or `text/csv` to auto-generate a schema from the file's columns — the first column becomes a query field and the rest become enriched fields (returns `202` once the file is accepted for processing). A schema must include 1-3 query fields and at least one enriched field, up to 25 fields total, with unique (case-insensitive) field names. Schemas created through the API are always `CSV`, and an account may have at most 25 CSV schemas. CSV uploads are limited to 10 MB.

<!-- theme: warning -->

> ### Early Access
> This API is in Early Access and may change at any time. Contact your PagerDuty account team to request access.

Scoped OAuth requires: `contextual_data.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "integration_type": "CSV",
  "name": "Application Environment Enrichment",
  "description": "Maps applications to team and runbook info by environment",
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "Application",
      "type": "query"
    },
    {
      "name": "Environment",
      "type": "query"
    },
    {
      "name": "Manager",
      "type": "enriched"
    },
    {
      "name": "Team",
      "type": "enriched"
    },
    {
      "name": "Runbook URL",
      "type": "enriched"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-enrichment-schema-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|filename|query|string|false|The filename for the CSV content. Required when creating a schema from a `text/csv` body; optional for `text/csv` record uploads. Ignored for `multipart/form-data` and JSON requests.|
|body|body|object|true|The enrichment schema to create. Provide a JSON body to define the schema explicitly, or upload a CSV file (as `multipart/form-data` or `text/csv`) to auto-generate a schema in which the first column becomes the query field and the remaining columns become enriched fields. CSV uploads are limited to 10 MB.|
|» integration_type|body|string|false|The schema source. Only `CSV` is supported through the API; the schema is always recorded as `CSV` regardless of the value sent.|
|» name|body|string|true|Display name of the enrichment schema.|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of this set of enrichment data.|
|» fields|body|[object]|true|The schema fields. Must include 1-3 query fields and at least one enriched field, up to 25 fields total. Field names must be unique (case-insensitive).|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the field. Must be unique within the schema (case-insensitive).|
|» » type|body|string|true|How the field is used. `query` fields match incoming events to records (case-insensitive); `enriched` fields carry the data added to a matched event.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|
|» integration_type|CSV|
|» » type|query|
|» » type|enriched|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
  "schema": {
    "id": "9f194d8d-0f58-4c5c-b1d2-a5adf7171821",
    "type": "enrichment_schema",
    "integration_type": "CSV",
    "name": "Team Lead and Runbooks",
    "description": "Attaches SME and Runbook URLs to Incident",
    "fields": [
      {
        "name": "Application",

      },
      {
        "name": "Manager",

      },
      {

      }
    ],
```

## Upload CSV records

<a id="opIduploadEnrichmentCsv"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/enrichment/schemas/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/records \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /enrichment/schemas/{schema_id}/records`

Uploads a CSV file of enrichment records into an existing schema, as `multipart/form-data` or `text/csv`. The file is accepted for asynchronous processing (returns `202`) and is limited to 10 MB. The CSV columns must align with the schema's fields: missing columns result in empty values and extra columns are ignored. Records are keyed by their query-field values, so uploading a row whose query values match an existing record updates that record.

<!-- theme: warning -->

> ### Early Access
> This API is in Early Access and may change at any time. Contact your PagerDuty account team to request access.

Scoped OAuth requires: `contextual_data.write`


> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
```

<h3 id="upload-csv-records-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|schema_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The ID of the enrichment schema.|
|filename|query|string|false|The filename for the CSV content. Required when creating a schema from a `text/csv` body; optional for `text/csv` record uploads. Ignored for `multipart/form-data` and JSON requests.|
|body|body|object|true|The CSV file to upload into the schema, as `multipart/form-data` or `text/csv`. The file is streamed for asynchronous processing and is limited to 10 MB. The CSV columns must align with the schema's fields: missing columns result in empty values and extra columns are ignored. Records are keyed by their query-field values, so uploading a row whose query values match an existing record updates that record.|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The CSV file to upload (max 10 MB).|

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-escalation-policies">Escalation Policies</h1>

Escalation policies define which user should be alerted at which time.


## List escalation policies

<a id="opIdlistEscalationPolicies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/escalation_policies \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /escalation_policies`

List all of the existing escalation policies.

Escalation policies define which user should be alerted at which time.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#escalation-policies)

Scoped OAuth requires: `escalation_policies.read`


<h3 id="list-escalation-policies-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results per page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Offset to start pagination search results.|
|total|query|boolean|false|By default the `total` field in pagination responses is set to `null` to provide the fastest possible response times. Set `total` to `true` for this field to be populated.<br><br>See our [Pagination Docs](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for more information.<br>|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|query|query|string|false|Filters the result, showing only the records whose name matches the query.|
|user_ids[]|query|[string]|false|Filters the results, showing only escalation policies on which any of the users is a target.|
|team_ids[]|query|[string]|false|An array of team IDs. Only results related to these teams will be returned. Account must have the `teams` ability to use this parameter.|
|include[]|query|string|false|Array of additional Models to include in response.|
|sort_by|query|string|false|Used to specify the field you wish to sort the results on.|

## Create an escalation policy

<a id="opIdcreateEscalationPolicy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/escalation_policies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "escalation_policy": {
      "type": "escalation_policy",
      "name": "Engineering Escalation Policy",
      "escalation_rules": [
        {
          "escalation_delay_in_minutes": 30,
          "targets": [
            {
              "id": "PEYSGVF",
              "type": "user_reference"
            }
          ],
          "escalation_rule_assignment_strategy": {
            "type": "round_robin"
          }
        }
      ],
      "services": [
        {
          "id": "PIJ90N7",
          "type": "service_reference"
        }
      ],
      "num_loops": 2,
      "on_call_handoff_notifications": "if_has_services",
      "teams": [
        {
          "id": "PQ9K7I8",
          "type": "team_reference"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Here is the ep for the engineering team."
    }
  }'
```

`POST /escalation_policies`

Creates a new escalation policy. At least one escalation rule must be provided.

Escalation policies define which user should be alerted at which time.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#escalation-policies)

Scoped OAuth requires: `escalation_policies.write`

`GET /escalation_policies/{id}/audit/records`

The returned records are sorted by the `execution_time` from newest to oldest.

See [`Cursor-based pagination`](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for instructions on how to paginate through the result set.

For more information see the [Audit API Document](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/audit-records-api/).

Scoped OAuth requires: `audit_records.read`


<h3 id="list-audit-records-for-an-escalation-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The minimum of the `limit` parameter used in the request or the maximum request size of the API.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Optional parameter used to request the "next" set of results from an API.  The value provided here is most commonly obtained from the `next_cursor` field of the previous request.  When no value is provided, the request starts at the beginning of the result set.<br>|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the date range over which you want to search. If not specified, defaults to `now() - 24 hours` (past 24 hours)|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the date range over which you want to search. If not specified, defaults to `now()`. May not be more than 31 days after `since`.|

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-event-enrichments">Event Enrichments</h1>

Event Enrichments allow you to automatically add contextual data to events as they're ingested, so that relevant information is available throughout the event, alert, and incident lifecycle. By leveraging the Contextual Data Platform (CDP), you can define rules that extract values from events or query enrichment schemas to populate event fields.

<!-- theme: warning -->

> ### Early Access
> This API is in Early Access and may change at any time before General Availability. Contact your PagerDuty account team to request access.


## List Event Enrichments

<a id="opIdlistEventEnrichments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/enrichment/event_enrichments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /enrichment/event_enrichments`

Event Enrichments allow you to automatically add contextual data to events as they're ingested, so that relevant information is available throughout the event, alert, and incident lifecycle. By leveraging the Contextual Data Platform (CDP), you can define rules that extract values from events or query enrichment schemas to populate event fields.

<!-- theme: warning -->

> ### Early Access
> This API is in Early Access and may change at any time. Contact your PagerDuty account team to request access.
