`PUT /enrichment/event_enrichments/{id}`

Event Enrichments allow you to automatically add contextual data to events as they're ingested, so that relevant information is available throughout the event, alert, and incident lifecycle. By leveraging the Contextual Data Platform (CDP), you can define rules that extract values from events or query enrichment schemas to populate event fields.

Event Enrichments allow you to automatically add contextual data to events as they're ingested, so that relevant information is available throughout the event, alert, and incident lifecycle. Event Enrichments allow you to automatically add contextual data to events as they're ingested, so that relevant information is available throughout the event, alert, and incident lifecycle. By leveraging the Contextual Data Platform (CDP), you can define rules that extract values from events or query enrichment schemas to populate event fields.

Associating an Event Orchestration or Service with an Event Enrichment allows for the enrichment to be evaluated when events are ingested for that Event Orchestration or Service

## Update Event Enrichment rules

<a id="opIdupdateEventEnrichmentRules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/enrichment/event_enrichments/string/rules \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "orchestration_path": {
      "sets": [
        {
          "id": "start",
          "rules": [
            {
              "label": "Extract server name from event source",
              "conditions": [
                {
                  "expression": "event.summary matches part '\''Application:'\''"
                }
              ],
              "actions": {
                "extractions": [
                  {
                    "target": "event.custom_details.server_name",
                    "template": "[production] {{event.source}}"
                  }
                ]
              }
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /enrichment/event_enrichments/{id}/rules`

Event Enrichments allow you to automatically add contextual data to events as they're ingested, so that relevant information is available throughout the event, alert, and incident lifecycle. By leveraging the Contextual Data Platform (CDP), you can define rules that extract values from events or query enrichment schemas to populate event fields.

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-event-orchestrations">Event Orchestrations</h1>

Event Orchestrations allow you to route events to an endpoint and create collections of Event Orchestrations, which define sets of actions to take based on event content.


## List Event Orchestrations

<a id="opIdlistEventOrchestrations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/event_orchestrations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /event_orchestrations`

List all Global Event Orchestrations on an Account.

Global Event Orchestrations allow you define a set of Global Rules and Router Rules, so that when you ingest events using the Orchestration's Routing Key your events will have actions applied via the Global Rules & then routed to the correct Service by the Router Rules, based on the event's content.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#event-orchestrations)

Scoped OAuth requires: `event_orchestrations.read`

## Create an Orchestration

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/event_orchestrations \
```

`POST /event_orchestrations`

Create a Global Event Orchestration.

Global Event Orchestrations allow you define a set of Global Rules and Router Rules, so that when you ingest events using the Orchestration's Routing Key your events will have actions applied via the Global Rules & then routed to the correct Service by the Router Rules, based on the event's content.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#event-orchestrations)

Scoped OAuth requires: `event_orchestrations.write`


> Body parameter

```json
    "team": {
      "id": "PXD0WR8"
    }
  }
}
```

## Migrate an Integration from one Event Orchestration to another

<a id="opIdmigrateOrchestrationIntegration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/event_orchestrations/string/integrations/migration \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "source_type": "orchestration",
    "source_id": "b02e973d-9620-4e0a-9edc-00fedf7d4694",
    "integration_id": "11832872-88b6-4661-8972-db5712b69496"
  }'
```

`POST /event_orchestrations/{id}/integrations/migration`

Move an Integration and its Routing Key from the Event Orchestration specified in the request payload, to the Event Orchestration specified in the request URL.

Any future events sent to this Integration's Routing Key will be processed by this Event Orchestration's Rules.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#event-orchestrations)

Scoped OAuth requires: `event_orchestrations.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "source_type": "orchestration",
  "source_id": "b02e973d-9620-4e0a-9edc-00fedf7d4694",
  "integration_id": "11832872-88b6-4661-8972-db5712b69496"
}
```

## Get the Global Orchestration for an Event Orchestration

<a id="opIdgetOrchPathGlobal"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/event_orchestrations/string/global \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /event_orchestrations/{id}/global`

Get the Global Orchestration for an Event Orchestration.

Global Orchestration Rules allows you to create a set of Event Rules. These rules evaluate against all Events sent to an Event Orchestration. When a matching rule is found, it can modify and enhance the event and can route the event to another set of Global Rules within this Orchestration for further processing.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#event-orchestrations)

Scoped OAuth requires: `event_orchestrations.read`


<h3 id="get-the-global-orchestration-for-an-event-orchestration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of an Event Orchestration.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "orchestration_path": {
    "type": "global",
    "parent": {
      "id": "b02e973d-9620-4e0a-9edc-00fedf7d4694",
      "self": "https://api.pagerduty.com/event_orchestrations/b02e973d-9620-4e0a-9edc-00fedf7d4694",
      "type": "event_orchestration_reference"
    },
    "self": "https://api.pagerduty.com/event_orchestrations/b02e973d-9620-4e0a-9edc-00fedf7d4694/global",
    "sets": [
      {
        "id": "start",
        "rules": [
          {
            "label": "Always apply some consistent event transformations to all events",
            "id": "c91f72f3",
            "conditions": [],
            "actions": {
              "variables": [
                {
                  "name": "hostname",
                  "path": "event.component",
                  "value": "hostname: (.*)",
                  "type": "regex"
                }
              ],
              "extractions": [
                {
                  "template": "{{variables.hostname}}",
                  "target": "event.custom_details.hostname"
                },
                {
                  "source": "event.source",
                  "regex": "www (.*) service",
                  "target": "event.source"
                }
              ],
              "incident_custom_field_updates": [
                {
                  "id": "PEXCK89",
                  "value": "#my-team-channel"
                },
                {
                  "id": "PN1C4A2",
                  "value": "{{event.timestamp}}"
                }
              ],
              "route_to": "step-two"
            }
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "id": "step-two",
        "rules": [
          {
            "label": "All critical alerts should be treated as P1 incidents",
            "id": "7c54529d",
            "conditions": [
              {
                "expression": "event.severity matches 'critical'"
              }
            ],
            "actions": {
              "priority": "P0IN2KQ",
              "suppress": false,
              "incident_custom_field_updates": [
                {
                  "id": "PEXCK89",

                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {

              }
            ],
            "actions": {

              }
            ],
            "actions": {
              "suppress": true
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "catch_all": {
      "actions": {
        "suppress": true,
        "incident_custom_field_updates": [
          {
            "id": "PEXCK89",
            "value": "#general-incident-notifications"
          }
        ]
      }
    },
```

## Get the Router for an Event Orchestration

<a id="opIdgetOrchPathRouter"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/event_orchestrations/string/router \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /event_orchestrations/{id}/router`

Get a Global Orchestration's Routing Rules.

An Orchestration Router allows you to create a set of Event Rules. The Router evaluates Events you send to this Global Orchestration against each of its rules, one at a time, and routes the event to a specific Service based on the first rule that matches. If an event doesn't match any rules, it'll be sent to service specified in as the `catch_all` or the "Unrouted" Orchestration if no service is specified.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#event-orchestrations)

Scoped OAuth requires: `event_orchestrations.read`


<h3 id="get-the-router-for-an-event-orchestration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of an Event Orchestration.|

## Update the Router for an Event Orchestration

<a id="opIdupdateOrchPathRouter"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/event_orchestrations/string/router \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "orchestration_path": {
      "sets": [
        {
          "id": "start",
          "rules": [
            {
              "label": "Dynamically route events",
              "id": "763110d0",
              "actions": {
                "dynamic_route_to": {
                  "source": "event.custom_details.pd_service",
                  "regex": ".*",
                  "lookup_by": "service_name"
                }
              }
            },
            {
              "label": "Events relating to our relational database",
              "id": "1c26698b",
              "conditions": [
                {
                  "expression": "event.summary matches part '\''database'\''"
                },
                {
                  "expression": "event.source matches regex '\''db[0-9]+-server'\''"
                }
              ],
              "actions": {
                "route_to": "PB31XBA"
              }
            },
            {
              "label": "Events relating to our www app server",
              "id": "d9801904",
              "conditions": [
                {
                  "expression": "event.summary matches part '\''www'\''"
                }
              ],
              "actions": {
                "route_to": "PC2D9ML"
              }
            },
            {
              "label": "Events relating to our delivery pipeline",
              "id": "ed624931",
              "conditions": [
                {
                  "expression": "trigger_count over 1 minute > 3"
                }
              ],
              "actions": {
                "route_to": "PQSJBMA"
              }
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /event_orchestrations/{id}/router`

Update a Global Orchestration's Routing Rules.

An Orchestration Router allows you to create a set of Event Rules. The Router evaluates Events you send to this Global Orchestration against each of its rules, one at a time, and routes the event to a specific Service based on the first rule that matches. If an event doesn't match any rules, it'll be sent to service specified in as the `catch_all` or the "Unrouted" Orchestration if no service is specified.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#event-orchestrations)

## Get the Unrouted Orchestration for an Event Orchestration

<a id="opIdgetOrchPathUnrouted"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/event_orchestrations/string/unrouted \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /event_orchestrations/{id}/unrouted`

Get a Global Event Orchestration's Rules for Unrouted events.

An Unrouted Orchestration allows you to create a set of Event Rules that will be evaluated against all events that don't match any rules in the Global Orchestration's Router. Events that reach the Unrouted Orchestration will never be routed to a specific Service.

The Unrouted Orchestration evaluates Events sent to it against each of its rules, beginning with the rules in the "start" set. When a matching rule is found, it can modify and enhance the event and can route the event to another set of rules within this Unrouted Orchestration for further processing.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#event-orchestrations)

Scoped OAuth requires: `event_orchestrations.read`


<h3 id="get-the-unrouted-orchestration-for-an-event-orchestration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of an Event Orchestration.|

```bash
  -d '{
    "orchestration_path": {
      "sets": [
        {
          "id": "start",

              "label": "Update the summary of un-matched Critical alerts so they'\''re easier to spot",

                }
```

`PUT /event_orchestrations/{id}/unrouted`

Update a Global Event Orchestration's Rules for Unrouted events.

An Unrouted Orchestration allows you to create a set of Event Rules that will be evaluated against all events that don't match any rules in the Global Orchestration's Router. Events that reach the Unrouted Orchestration will never be routed to a specific Service.

The Unrouted Orchestration evaluates Events sent to it against each of its rules, beginning with the rules in the "start" set. When a matching rule is found, it can modify and enhance the event and can route the event to another set of rules within this Unrouted Orchestration for further processing.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#event-orchestrations)

## Get the Service Orchestration for a Service

<a id="opIdgetOrchPathService"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/event_orchestrations/services/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /event_orchestrations/services/{service_id}`

Get a Service Orchestration.

A Service Orchestration allows you to create a set of Event Rules. The Service Orchestration evaluates Events sent to this Service against each of its rules, beginning with the rules in the "start" set. When a matching rule is found, it can modify and enhance the event and can route the event to another set of rules within this Service Orchestration for further processing.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#event-orchestrations)

Scoped OAuth requires: `services.read`


<h3 id="get-the-service-orchestration-for-a-service-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|service_id|path|string|true|The service ID|
|include[]|query|string|false|Array of additional Models to include in response.|

## Update the Service Orchestration for a Service

<a id="opIdupdateOrchPathService"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/event_orchestrations/services/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "orchestration_path": {
      "sets": [
        {
          "id": "start",
          "rules": [
            {
              "label": "Always apply some consistent event transformations to all events",
              "id": "c91f72f3",
              "conditions": [],
              "actions": {
                "variables": [
                  {
                    "name": "hostname",
                    "path": "event.component",
                    "value": "hostname: (.*)",
                    "type": "regex"
                  }
                ],
                "extractions": [
                  {
                    "template": "{{variables.hostname}}",
                    "target": "event.custom_details.hostname"
                  },
                  {
                    "source": "event.source",
                    "regex": "www (.*) service",
                    "target": "event.source"
                  }
                ],
                "pagerduty_automation_actions": [
                  {
                    "action_id": "01CSB5SMOKCKVRI5GN0LJG7SMB",
                    "trigger_types": [
                      "alert_triggered"
                    ]
                  }
                ],
                "incident_custom_field_updates": [
                  {
                    "id": "PEXCK89",
                    "value": "#my-team-channel"
                  },
                  {
                    "id": "PN1C4A2",
                    "value": "{{event.timestamp}}"
                  }
                ],
                "route_to": "step-two"
              }
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "id": "step-two",
          "rules": [
            {
              "label": "All critical alerts should be treated as P1 incidents",
              "id": "7c54529d",
              "conditions": [
                {
                  "expression": "event.severity matches '\''critical'\''"
                }
              ],
              "actions": {
                "annotate": "Please use our P1 runbook: https://docs.test/p1-runbook",
                "priority": "P0IN2KQ",
                "suppress": false,
                "incident_custom_field_updates": [
                  {
                    "id": "PEXCK89",
                    "value": "#p1-incident-response"
                  }
                ]
              }
            },
            {
              "label": "If there'\''s something wrong on the canary let the team know about it in our deployments Slack channel",
              "id": "1f6d9a33",
              "conditions": [
                {
                  "expression": "event.custom_details.hostname matches part '\''canary'\''"
                }
              ],
              "actions": {
                "automation_actions": [
                  {
                    "name": "Canary Slack Notification",
                    "url": "https://our-slack-listerner.test/send-notification",
                    "auto_send": true,
                    "headers": [
                      {
                        "key": "X-Notification-Source",
                        "value": "PagerDuty Incident Webhook"
                      }
                    ],
                    "parameters": [
                      {
                        "key": "channel",
                        "value": "#my-team-channel"
                      },
                      {
                        "key": "message",
                        "value": "Something is wrong with the canary deployment"
                      }
                    ],
                    "trigger_types": [
                      "alert_triggered"
                    ]
                  }
                ],
                "incident_custom_field_updates": [
                  {
                    "id": "PEXCK89",
                    "value": "#my-team-channel"
                  }
                ]
              }
            },
            {
              "label": "Pause the alert and trigger a reboot action if flaky server receives an error",
              "id": "c0163dbe",
              "conditions": [
                {
                  "expression": "event.custom_details.hostname matches part '\''staging'\''"
                }
              ],
              "actions": {
                "suspend": 300,
                "pagerduty_automation_actions": [
                  {
                    "action_id": "01CSBCGJXMG7ABIJZKPD8P9RCL",
                    "trigger_types": [
                      "alert_suspended"
                    ]
                  }
                ]
              }
            },
            {
              "label": "Never bother the on-call for info-level events outside of work hours",
              "id": "cd770384",
              "conditions": [
                {
                  "expression": "event.severity matches '\''info'\'' and not (now in Mon,Tue,Wed,Thu,Fri 09:00:00 to 17:00:00 America/Los_Angeles)"
                }
              ],
              "actions": {
                "suppress": true
              }
            }
          ]
        }
      ],
      "catch_all": {
        "actions": {
          "suppress": true
        },
        "incident_custom_field_updates": [
          {
            "id": "PEXCK89",
            "value": "#general-incident-notifications"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /event_orchestrations/services/{service_id}`

Update a Service Orchestration.

A Service Orchestration allows you to create a set of Event Rules. The Service Orchestration evaluates Events sent to this Service against each of its rules, beginning with the rules in the "start" set. When a matching rule is found, it can modify and enhance the event and can route the event to another set of rules within this Service Orchestration for further processing.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#event-orchestrations)

Scoped OAuth requires: `services.write`

## Update a Cache Variable for a Service Event Orchestration

<a id="opIdupdateCacheVarOnServiceOrch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/event_orchestrations/services/string/cache_variables/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{

        }

  }'
```

## List Enablements for an Event Orchestration

<a id="opIdlistEventOrchestrationFeatureEnablements"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/event_orchestrations/string/enablements \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /event_orchestrations/{id}/enablements`

List all feature enablement settings for an Event Orchestration. Currently, only the `aiops` enablement is supported.

For any account with the AIOps product addon, every Event Orchestration will have AIOps features enabled by default.

**Warning conditions**:
- If the account is not entitled to use AIOps features, a warning will be returned alongside the enablement data.

For PDRP customers, this feature is branded **Signal Intelligence** in the PagerDuty product UI. The API field names and values (e.g. `aiops`) are unchanged.

Scoped OAuth requires: `event_orchestrations.read`

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|

```json
  "enablements": [
    {
      "feature": "aiops",
      "enabled": true,
      "updated_at": "2025-04-25T15:00:00Z"

  ]
}
```

## Update an Enablement for an Event Orchestration

<a id="opIdupdateEventOrchestrationFeatureEnablements"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/event_orchestrations/string/enablements/aiops \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "enablement": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /event_orchestrations/{id}/enablements/{feature_name}`

Update the feature enablement setting for a specific product addon on an Event Orchestration. This setting controls enabling or disabling the set of features contained within the addon.
Currently, only `aiops` is supported as a valid feature enablement.

**Warning conditions**:
- If the account is not entitled to use AIOps features, the setting will be updated, but a warning will be returned.

For PDRP customers, this feature is branded **Signal Intelligence** in the PagerDuty product UI. The API field names and values (e.g. `aiops`) are unchanged.

Scoped OAuth requires: `event_orchestrations.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enablement": {
    "enabled": true
  }
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of an Event Orchestration.|
|feature_name|path|string|true|The feature enablement identifier, typically the name of the product addon. Currently only `aiops` is supported. For PDRP customers, this feature is branded **Signal Intelligence** in the PagerDuty product UI. The API field names and values (e.g. `aiops`) are unchanged.|
|body|body|object|false|The feature enablement setting to apply.|

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/extensions/string/enable \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /extensions/{id}/enable`

Enable an extension that is temporarily disabled. (This API does not require a request body.)

Extensions are representations of Extension Schema objects that are attached to Services.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#extensions)

Scoped OAuth requires: `extensions.write`

|---|---|---|---|---|

|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-incidents">Incidents</h1>

An incident represents a problem or an issue that needs to be addressed and resolved. Incidents trigger on a service, which prompts notifications to go out to on-call responders per the service's escalation policy.


## List incidents

<a id="opIdlistIncidents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /incidents`

List existing incidents.

An incident represents a problem or an issue that needs to be addressed and resolved.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#incidents)

Scoped OAuth requires: `incidents.read`


<h3 id="list-incidents-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results per page. Maximum of 100.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Offset to start pagination search results.|
|total|query|boolean|false|By default the `total` field in pagination responses is set to `null` to provide the fastest possible response times. Set `total` to `true` for this field to be populated.<br><br>See our [Pagination Docs](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for more information.<br>|
|date_range|query|string|false|When set to all, the since and until parameters and defaults are ignored.|
|incident_key|query|string|false|Incident de-duplication key. Incidents with child alerts do not have an incident key; querying by incident key will return incidents whose alerts have alert_key matching the given incident key.|
|service_ids[]|query|[string]|false|Returns only the incidents associated with the passed service(s). This expects one or more service IDs.|
|team_ids[]|query|[string]|false|An array of team IDs. Only results related to these teams will be returned. Account must have the `teams` ability to use this parameter.|
|user_ids[]|query|[string]|false|Returns only the incidents currently assigned to the passed user(s). This expects one or more user IDs. Note: When using the assigned_to_user filter, you will only receive incidents with statuses of triggered or acknowledged. This is because resolved incidents are not assigned to any user.|
|urgencies[]|query|string|false|Array of the urgencies of the incidents to be returned. Defaults to all urgencies. Account must have the `urgencies` ability to do this.|
|time_zone|query|string(tzinfo)|false|Time zone used to render timestamps and to interpret `since/until` values before filtering. Rendering defaults to UTC if omitted. `since/until` default to the account's time zone if omitted.|
|statuses[]|query|string|false|Return only incidents with the given statuses. To query multiple statuses, pass `statuses[]` more than once, for example: `https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents?statuses[]=triggered&statuses[]=acknowledged`. (More status codes may be introduced in the future.)|
|sort_by|query|[string]|false|Used to specify both the field you wish to sort the results on (incident_number/created_at/resolved_at/urgency), as well as the direction (asc/desc) of the results. The sort_by field and direction should be separated by a colon. A maximum of two fields can be included, separated by a comma. Sort direction defaults to ascending. The account must have the `urgencies` ability to sort by the urgency.|
|include[]|query|string|false|Array of additional details to include.|
|since|query|string|false|The start of the date range over which you want to search. Maximum range is 6 months and default is 1 month.|
|until|query|string|false|The end of the date range over which you want to search. Maximum range is 6 months and default is 1 month.|

|urgencies[]|high|
|urgencies[]|low|

|statuses[]|resolved|

|include[]|teams|
|include[]|users|

## Manage incidents

<a id="opIdupdateIncidents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'From: user@example.com' \
  -d '{
    "incidents": [
      {
        "id": "PT4KHLK",
        "type": "incident_reference",
        "status": "acknowledged"
      },
      {
        "id": "PQMF62U",
        "type": "incident_reference",
        "priority": {
          "id": "P53ZZH5",
          "type": "priority_reference"
        }
      },
      {
        "id": "PPVZH9X",
        "type": "incident_reference",
        "status": "resolved"
      },
      {
        "id": "P8JOGX7",
        "type": "incident_reference",
        "assignments": [
          {
            "assignee": {
              "id": "PXPGF42",
              "type": "user_reference"
            }
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "id": "PYJ9K7I",
        "type": "incident_reference",
        "incident_type": {
          "name": "major_incident"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /incidents`

Acknowledge, resolve, escalate or reassign one or more incidents.

An incident represents a problem or an issue that needs to be addressed and resolved.

A maximum of 250 incidents may be updated at a time. If more than this number of incidents are given, the API will respond with status 413 (Request Entity Too Large).

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#incidents)

Scoped OAuth requires: `incidents.write`

This API operation has operation specific rate limits. See the [Rate Limits](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/72d3b724589e3-rest-api-rate-limits) page for more information.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "incidents": [
    {
      "id": "PT4KHLK",
      "type": "incident_reference",
      "status": "acknowledged"
    },
    {
      "id": "PQMF62U",
      "type": "incident_reference",
      "priority": {
        "id": "P53ZZH5",
        "type": "priority_reference"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "PPVZH9X",
      "type": "incident_reference",
      "status": "resolved"
    },
    {
      "id": "P8JOGX7",
      "type": "incident_reference",
      "assignments": [
        {
          "assignee": {
            "id": "PXPGF42",
            "type": "user_reference"
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "PYJ9K7I",
      "type": "incident_reference",
      "incident_type": {
        "name": "major_incident"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="manage-incidents-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results per page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Offset to start pagination search results.|
|total|query|boolean|false|By default the `total` field in pagination responses is set to `null` to provide the fastest possible response times. Set `total` to `true` for this field to be populated.<br><br>See our [Pagination Docs](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for more information.<br>|
|From|header|string(email)|true|The email address of a valid user associated with the account making the request.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» incidents|body|[object]|true|An array of incidents, including the parameters to update.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The id of the incident to update.|
|» » type|body|string|true|The incident type.|
|» » status|body|string|false|The new status of the incident. If the incident is currently resolved, setting the status to "triggered" or "acknowledged" will reopen it. When reopening an incident to the "triggered" status, it will be assigned based on the assignees or escalation_policy fields in the request, otherwise it will be assigned to the current Escalation Policy. When reopening an incident to the "acknowledged" status, it will be assigned to the current user.|
|» » resolution|body|string|false|The resolution for this incident. This field is used only when setting the incident status to resolved.<br>The value provided here is added to the incident’s 'Resolve' log entry as a note and will not be displayed directly in the UI.<br>|
|» » title|body|string|false|A succinct description of the nature, symptoms, cause, or effect of the incident.|
|» » priority|body|object \| string|false|The priority of the incident. Can be provided as a priority object or a string matching a priority name. If a string is provided, the highest priority with a matching name will be used.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » id|body|string|true|The ID of the priority.|
|» » » name|body|string|false|The user-provided short name of the priority.|
|» » » type|body|string|true|The type of the reference.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|A string matching the name of a priority. If provided, the highest priority with a matching name will be used.|
|» » escalation_level|body|integer|false|Escalate the incident to this level in the escalation policy.|
|» » assignments|body|[object]|false|Assign the incident to these assignees.|
|» » » assignee|body|[UserReference](#schemauserreference)|false|none|
|» » incident_type|body|[IncidentTypeReference](#schemaincidenttypereference)|false|none|
|» » escalation_policy|body|[EscalationPolicyReference](#schemaescalationpolicyreference)|false|none|
|» » urgency|body|string|false|The urgency of the incident.|
|» » conference_bridge|body|[ConferenceBridge](#schemaconferencebridge)|false|none|

## Create an Incident

<a id="opIdcreateIncident"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'From: user@example.com' \
  -d '{
    "incident": {
      "type": "incident",
      "title": "The server is on fire.",
      "service": {
        "id": "PWIXJZS",
        "type": "service_reference"
      },
      "priority": {
        "id": "P53ZZH5",
        "type": "priority_reference"
      },
      "urgency": "high",
      "incident_key": "baf7cf21b1da41b4b0221008339ff357",
      "body": {
        "type": "incident_body",
        "details": "A disk is getting full on this machine. You should investigate what is causing the disk to fill, and ensure that there is an automated process in place for ensuring data is rotated (eg. logs should have logrotate around them). If data is expected to stay on this disk forever, you should start planning to scale up to a larger disk."
      },
      "incident_type": {
        "name": "major_incident"
      },
      "escalation_policy": {
        "id": "PT20YPA",
        "type": "escalation_policy_reference"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /incidents`

Create an incident synchronously without a corresponding event from a monitoring service.

An incident represents a problem or an issue that needs to be addressed and resolved.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#incidents)

Scoped OAuth requires: `incidents.write`

This API operation has operation specific rate limits. See the [Rate Limits](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/72d3b724589e3-rest-api-rate-limits) page for more information.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "incident": {
    "type": "incident",
    "title": "The server is on fire.",
    "service": {
      "id": "PWIXJZS",
      "type": "service_reference"
    },
    "priority": {
      "id": "P53ZZH5",
      "type": "priority_reference"
    },
    "urgency": "high",
    "incident_key": "baf7cf21b1da41b4b0221008339ff357",
    "body": {
      "type": "incident_body",
      "details": "A disk is getting full on this machine. You should investigate what is causing the disk to fill, and ensure that there is an automated process in place for ensuring data is rotated (eg. logs should have logrotate around them). If data is expected to stay on this disk forever, you should start planning to scale up to a larger disk."
    },
    "incident_type": {
      "name": "major_incident"
    },
    "escalation_policy": {
      "id": "PT20YPA",
      "type": "escalation_policy_reference"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-incident-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|From|header|string(email)|true|The email address of a valid user associated with the account making the request.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» incident|body|object|true|Details of the incident to be created.|
|» » type|body|string|true|none|
|» » title|body|string|true|A succinct description of the nature, symptoms, cause, or effect of the incident.|
|» » service|body|[ServiceReference](#schemaservicereference)|true|none|
|» » priority|body|[PriorityReference](#schemapriorityreference)|false|none|
|» » urgency|body|string|false|The urgency of the incident|
|» » body|body|[IncidentBody](#schemaincidentbody)|false|none|
|» » incident_key|body|string|false|A string which identifies the incident. Sending subsequent requests referencing the same service and with the same incident_key will result in those requests being rejected if an open incident matches that incident_key.|
|» » assignments|body|[object]|false|Assign the incident to these assignees. Cannot be specified if an escalation policy is given.|
|» » » assignee|body|[UserReference](#schemauserreference)|false|none|
|» » incident_type|body|[IncidentTypeReference](#schemaincidenttypereference)|false|none|
|» » escalation_policy|body|[EscalationPolicyReference](#schemaescalationpolicyreference)|false|none|
|» » conference_bridge|body|[ConferenceBridge](#schemaconferencebridge)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|
|» » type|incident|
|» » urgency|high|
|» » urgency|low|

## Get an incident

<a id="opIdgetIncident"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /incidents/{id}`

Show detailed information about an incident. Accepts either an incident id, or an incident number.

An incident represents a problem or an issue that needs to be addressed and resolved.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#incidents)

Scoped OAuth requires: `incidents.read`

|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|
|include[]|query|string|false|Array of additional details to include.|

## Update an incident

<a id="opIdupdateIncident"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'From: user@example.com' \
  -d '{
    "incident": {
      "type": "incident_reference",
      "status": "acknowledged"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /incidents/{id}`

Acknowledge, resolve, escalate or reassign an incident.

An incident represents a problem or an issue that needs to be addressed and resolved.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#incidents)

Scoped OAuth requires: `incidents.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "incident": {
    "type": "incident_reference",
    "status": "acknowledged"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-incident-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|
|From|header|string(email)|true|The email address of a valid user associated with the account making the request.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» incident|body|object|true|The parameters of the incident to update.|
|» » type|body|string|true|The incident type.|
|» » status|body|string|false|The new status of the incident. If the incident is currently resolved, setting the status to "triggered" or "acknowledged" will reopen it. When reopening an incident to the "triggered" status, it will be assigned based on the assignees or escalation_policy fields in the request, otherwise it will be assigned to the current Escalation Policy. When reopening an incident to the "acknowledged" status, it will be assigned to the current user.|
|» » priority|body|object \| string|false|The priority of the incident. Can be provided as a priority object or a string matching a priority name. If a string is provided, the highest priority with a matching name will be used.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » » id|body|string|true|The ID of the priority.|
|» » » name|body|string|false|The user-provided short name of the priority.|
|» » » type|body|string|true|The type of the reference.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|A string matching the name of a priority. If provided, the highest priority with a matching name will be used.|
|» » resolution|body|string|false|The resolution for this incident. This field is used only when setting the incident status to resolved.<br>The value provided here is added to the incident’s 'Resolve' log entry as a note and will not be displayed directly in the UI.<br>|
|» » title|body|string|false|The new title of the incident.|
|» » escalation_level|body|integer|false|Escalate the incident to this level in the escalation policy.|
|» » assignments|body|[object]|false|Assign the incident to these assignees.|
|» » » assignee|body|[UserReference](#schemauserreference)|false|none|
|» » incident_type|body|[IncidentTypeReference](#schemaincidenttypereference)|false|none|
|» » escalation_policy|body|[EscalationPolicyReference](#schemaescalationpolicyreference)|false|none|
|» » urgency|body|string|false|The urgency of the incident.|
|» » conference_bridge|body|[ConferenceBridge](#schemaconferencebridge)|false|none|
|» » service|body|object|false|Assign the incident to this service.|
|» » » id|body|string|true|The ID of the service.|
|» » » type|body|string|true|The type of the reference.|

`GET /incidents/{id}/alerts`

List alerts for the specified incident.

An incident represents a problem or an issue that needs to be addressed and resolved.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#incidents)

Scoped OAuth requires: `incidents.read`

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results per page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Offset to start pagination search results.|
|total|query|boolean|false|By default the `total` field in pagination responses is set to `null` to provide the fastest possible response times. Set `total` to `true` for this field to be populated.<br><br>See our [Pagination Docs](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for more information.<br>|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|
|alert_key|query|string|false|Alert de-duplication key.|
|statuses[]|query|string|false|Return only alerts with the given statuses. (More status codes may be introduced in the future.)|
|sort_by|query|string|false|Used to specify both the field you wish to sort the results on (created_at/resolved_at), as well as the direction (asc/desc) of the results. The sort_by field and direction should be separated by a colon. A maximum of two fields can be included, separated by a comma. Sort direction defaults to ascending.|
|include[]|query|string|false|Array of additional details to include.|

## Manage alerts

<a id="opIdupdateIncidentAlerts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/string/alerts \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'From: user@example.com' \
  -d '{
    "alerts": [
      {
        "id": "PPVZH9X",
        "type": "alert",
        "status": "resolved"
      },
      {
        "id": "P8JOGX7",
        "type": "alert",
        "incident": {
          "id": "PPVZH9X",
          "type": "incident_reference"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /incidents/{id}/alerts`

Resolve multiple alerts or associate them with different incidents.

An incident represents a problem or an issue that needs to be addressed and resolved. An alert represents a digital signal that was emitted to PagerDuty by the monitoring systems that detected or identified the issue.

A maximum of 250 alerts may be updated at a time. If more than this number of alerts are given, the API will respond with status 413 (Request Entity Too Large).

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#incidents)

Scoped OAuth requires: `incidents.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "alerts": [
    {
      "id": "PPVZH9X",
      "type": "alert",
      "status": "resolved"
    },
    {
      "id": "P8JOGX7",
      "type": "alert",
      "incident": {
        "id": "PPVZH9X",
        "type": "incident_reference"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="manage-alerts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results per page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Offset to start pagination search results.|
|total|query|boolean|false|By default the `total` field in pagination responses is set to `null` to provide the fastest possible response times. Set `total` to `true` for this field to be populated.<br><br>See our [Pagination Docs](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for more information.<br>|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|
|From|header|string(email)|true|The email address of a valid user associated with the account making the request.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» alerts|body|[[AlertUpdate](#schemaalertupdate)]|true|An array of alerts, including the parameters to update for each alert.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|

```json
  "alerts": [
    {
      "id": "PT4KHLK",
      "type": "alert",
      "summary": "The server is on fire.",
      "self": "https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/PT4KHLK/alerts/PXPGF42",
```

## Merge incidents

<a id="opIdmergeIncidents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/string/merge \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'From: user@example.com' \
  -d '{
    "source_incidents": [
      {
        "id": "P8JOGX7",
        "type": "incident_reference"
      },
      {
        "id": "PPVZH9X",
        "type": "incident_reference"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /incidents/{id}/merge`

Merge a list of source incidents into the target [incident](https://developer.pagerduty.com/api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#incidents).

After the merge is performed the target incident will contain the source incidents' [alerts](https://developer.pagerduty.com/api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#alerts),
and the source incidents will be resolved.

Only incidents that have alerts or incidents that were created manually in the UI can be merged.

Open incidents cannot be merged into a resolved incident. The target incident must be open.

An incident cannot have more than 1000 alerts. The server will return an error if merging the source incidents
will result in the target incident having more than 1000 alerts.

Scoped OAuth requires: `incidents.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "source_incidents": [
    {
      "id": "P8JOGX7",
      "type": "incident_reference"
    },
    {
      "id": "PPVZH9X",
      "type": "incident_reference"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="merge-incidents-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|
|From|header|string(email)|true|The email address of a valid user associated with the account making the request.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» source_incidents|body|[[IncidentReference](#schemaincidentreference)]|true|The source incidents that will be merged into the target incident and resolved.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "incident": {
    "id": "PT4KHLK",
    "type": "incident_reference",
    "summary": "[#1234] The server is on fire.",
    "self": "https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/PT4KHLK",
    "html_url": "https://subdomain.pagerduty.com/incidents/PT4KHLK"
  }
}
```

```json
  "error": {
    "message": "Not Found",
    "code": 2100
  }
}
```

```json
  }
}
```

```json
  }
}
```

## Create a note on an incident

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/string/notes \
```

`POST /incidents/{id}/notes`

An incident represents a problem or an issue that needs to be addressed and resolved.

Past Incidents returns Incidents within the past 6 months that have similar metadata and were generated on the same Service as the parent Incident. By default, 5 Past Incidents are returned. Note: This feature is currently available as part of the Event Intelligence package or Digital Operations plan only.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#past_incidents)

## Create a responder request for an incident

<a id="opIdcreateIncidentResponderRequest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/string/responder_requests \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "requester_id": "PL1JMK5",
    "message": "Please help with issue - join bridge at +1(234)-567-8910",
    "responder_request_targets": [
      {
        "responder_request_target": {
          "id": "PJ25ZYX",
          "type": "user_reference"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /incidents/{id}/responder_requests`

Send a new responder request for the specified incident. This endpoint requires the account to have access to the [responder requests](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/add-responders) feature.

**Account Ability Requirement**: The account must have the `coordinated_responding` ability. Returns 402 Payment Required if the ability is missing. You can use the [List Abilities API](openapiv3.json/paths/~1abilities/get) to check account abilities.

A user or an escalation policy can be requested. The responder targets will be notified via their high urgency notification rules, until the target user has either accepted or declined the request.
Previous responder requests for a given target can be cancelled (preventing them from further notifying or escalating), with the [Cancel Responder Requests](openapiv3.json/paths/~1incidents~1{id}~1responder_requests~1cancel/put) endpoint.

Scoped OAuth requires: `incidents.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "requester_id": "PL1JMK5",
  "message": "Please help with issue - join bridge at +1(234)-567-8910",
  "responder_request_targets": [
    {
      "responder_request_target": {
        "id": "PJ25ZYX",
        "type": "user_reference"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» requester_id|body|string|true|The user id of the requester.|
|» message|body|string|true|The message sent with the responder request.|
|» responder_request_targets|body|[[ResponderRequestTargetReference](#schemaresponderrequesttargetreference)]|true|The array of targets the responder request is sent to.|

## Cancel responder requests for an incident

<a id="opIdcancelIncidentResponderRequest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/string/responder_requests/cancel \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "requester_id": "PL1JMK5",
    "responder_request_targets": [
      {
        "type": "user_reference",
        "id": "PJ25ZYX"
      },
      {
        "type": "escalation_policy_reference",
        "id": "PEP12AB"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /incidents/{id}/responder_requests/cancel`

Cancel pending responder requests for the specified incident.

This endpoint allows you to cancel responder requests for specified targets that are in a pending state. Only responders who have not yet joined or declined can be cancelled. This endpoint requires the account to have access to the [responder requests](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/add-responders) feature.

**Account Ability Requirement**: The account must have the `coordinated_responding` ability. Returns 402 Payment Required if the ability is missing. You can use the [List Abilities API](openapiv3.json/paths/~1abilities/get) to check account abilities.

**State Constraints**: Only responders in the `pending` state can be cancelled. Responders who have already `joined` or `declined` are not affected (the result will indicate their current state).

**User vs Escalation Policy Behavior**:
- **Users**: Direct cancellation, updates state to `user_cancelled`, stops notifications
- **Escalation Policies**: Stops the escalation process, updates state of all pending users from that escalation policy to `user_cancelled` and stops notifications

**Result Values**:
- `cancelled`: Successfully cancelled
- `joined`: User already joined (not cancelled)
- `declined`: User already declined (not cancelled)
- `not_found`: Target not found or not part of any responder request

Scoped OAuth requires: `incidents.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "requester_id": "PL1JMK5",
  "responder_request_targets": [
    {
      "type": "user_reference",
      "id": "PJ25ZYX"
    },
    {
      "type": "escalation_policy_reference",
      "id": "PEP12AB"
    }
  ]
}
```

|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» requester_id|body|string|true|The user id of the requester.|
|» responder_request_targets|body|[object]|true|The array of targets to cancel.|
|» » type|body|string|true|The type of target (either a user or an escalation policy)|
|» » id|body|string|true|The id of the user or escalation policy|

#### Enumerated Values

## Get Scribe transcripts for an incident

<a id="opIdgetIncidentScribeTranscripts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/string/scribe_transcripts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /incidents/{id}/scribe_transcripts`

Get download links for the Scribe transcripts of the specified incident. Only Scribes that have completed are returned; a Scribe that is still in progress does not appear in the response.

Each entry contains a presigned `download_url` for a single transcript format, selected with the `format` query parameter (`enhanced` by default, or `raw`). 

The `download_url` is time-limited and expires after one hour, so request a new one if it has expired. `download_url` is `null` when the transcript is not available for the requested format.

Scoped OAuth requires: `incidents.read`


<h3 id="get-scribe-transcripts-for-an-incident-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|
|format|query|string|false|The transcript format to return a download link for.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|
|format|enhanced|
|format|raw|

## Create a status update on an incident

<a id="opIdcreateIncidentStatusUpdate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/string/status_updates \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -H 'From: user@example.com' \
  -d '{

    "subject": "Server Fire Update",
    "html_message": "<h1>Server is still on fire</h1>"
  }'
```

`POST /incidents/{id}/status_updates`

Create a new status update for the specified incident. Optionally pass `subject` and `html_message` properties in the request body to override the email notification that gets sent.

An incident represents a problem or an issue that needs to be addressed and resolved.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#incidents)

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-incident-reviews">Incident Reviews</h1>

An Incident Review is a structured, post-resolution record of what happened during an Incident: what the impact was, how it was handled, and what should change as a result. Each Incident has at most one Incident Review, and its sections are determined by the template the Incident Review follows.


## List Incident Reviews

<a id="opIdlistIncidentReviews"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/reviews \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /incidents/reviews`

List the Incident Reviews on the account, newest first by creation time.

Only Incident Reviews on Incidents the caller can see are returned. Each entry is a summary; fetch the Incident Review by its Incident to get its sections.

This endpoint uses cursor pagination. Omit `cursor` for the first page, then pass the `next_cursor` from the previous response until it is `null`.

Scoped OAuth requires: `incident_reviews.read`


<h3 id="list-incident-reviews-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|status|query|[string]|false|Only return Incident Reviews with one of these statuses. Repeat the parameter to pass more than one.|
|status_not|query|[string]|false|Exclude Incident Reviews with any of these statuses. Repeat the parameter to pass more than one.|

## Update an Incident Review

<a id="opIdupdateIncidentReview"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/string/review \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Database outage review",
    "status": "completed"
  }'
```

`PUT /incidents/{id}/review`

Update the Incident Review for the specified Incident.

This is a partial update: an omitted field leaves the current value unchanged.

Moving `status` to `completed` is rejected with `409` while any required section is still unfilled.

On accounts where completed Incident Reviews are read-only, any other change to a `completed` Incident Review is rejected with `409` until it is reopened by setting `status` to another value. Completing or reopening an Incident Review requires permission to complete it, or the request is rejected with `403`.

`409` is also returned if the Incident Review is locked, or if it uses a format this version of the API cannot edit.

Scoped OAuth requires: `incident_reviews.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "Database outage review",
  "status": "completed"
}
```

|» title|body|string|false|The updated title of the Incident Review.|
|» status|body|string|false|The updated status of the Incident Review.|

## Create an Incident Review

<a id="opIdcreateIncidentReview"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/string/review \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Database outage review"
  }'
```

`POST /incidents/{id}/review`

Create an Incident Review for the specified Incident.

An Incident can have at most one Incident Review, so this returns `400` if the Incident already has one. A caller that wants create-or-fetch behaviour should fall back to `GET` on failure.

The new Incident Review follows the account's default template, which determines its sections.

When called with a User API token, the caller owns the new Incident Review. An account API key may name an owner with `owner_user_id`.

Returns `400` if `owner_user_id` is not a User on the account, or if a User API token names someone other than the caller.

Scoped OAuth requires: `incident_reviews.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "Database outage review"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-incident-review-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» title|body|string|true|The title of the Incident Review.|
|» owner_user_id|body|string|false|The ID of the User who should own the Incident Review. Only for account API keys, whose Incident Reviews would otherwise have no owner; with a User API token the caller is the owner, and naming anyone else is rejected with `400`. The User must belong to the account. Ignored unless the account has per-review permissions.<br>|

## List action items for an Incident Review

<a id="opIdlistIncidentReviewActionItems"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/string/review/action_items \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /incidents/{id}/review/action_items`

List the action items on the Incident Review for the specified Incident, oldest first by creation time.

Returns an empty list for an Incident Review that has no action items, and `404` when the Incident has no Incident Review, or if the caller cannot see it.

This endpoint uses cursor pagination. Omit `cursor` for the first page, then pass the `next_cursor` from the previous response until it is `null`.

Scoped OAuth requires: `incident_reviews.read`

## Add a marker to an Incident Review timeline

<a id="opIdcreateIncidentReviewMarker"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/string/review/markers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "title": "Customer-reported timeline update",
    "type": "Key Moment",
    "notes": [
      "Customer confirmed impact started at 10:42 UTC"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /incidents/{id}/review/markers`

Add a marker to the timeline of the Incident Review for the specified Incident.

A marker highlights a point of interest on the timeline. Each entry in `notes` is added as its own event attached to the new marker.

Returns `404` when the Incident has no Incident Review, or if the caller cannot see it, and `409` when the Incident Review is `completed` and must be reopened first.

`409` is also returned if the Incident Review is locked, or if it uses a format this version of the API cannot edit.

Scoped OAuth requires: `incident_reviews.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "Customer-reported timeline update",
  "type": "Key Moment",
  "notes": [
    "Customer confirmed impact started at 10:42 UTC"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-marker-to-an-incident-review-timeline-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» title|body|string|true|The title of the marker.|
|» type|body|string|false|The name of an existing marker type. Defaults to `Key Moment` if omitted.|
|» notes|body|[string]|true|One or more notes to attach to the marker as supporting evidence. Each note becomes its own event on the marker.|

|Content-Type|application/json|

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-incident-types">Incident Types</h1>

Incident Types are a feature which will allow customers to categorize incidents, such as a security incident, a major incident, or a fraud incident.


## List incident types

<a id="opIdlistIncidentTypes"></a>

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /incidents/types`

List the available incident types

Incident Types are a feature which will allow customers to categorize incidents, such as a security incident, a major incident, or a fraud incident.
These can be filtered by enabled or disabled types.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#incidentType)

## Create an Incident Type

<a id="opIdcreateIncidentType"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/types \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "incident_type": {
      "name": "fraud_incident",
      "display_name": "Fraud Incident",
      "parent_type": "incident_default"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /incidents/types`

Create a new incident type.

Incident Types are a feature which will allow customers to categorize incidents, such as a security incident, a major incident, or a fraud incident.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#incidentType)

Scoped OAuth requires: `incident_types.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "incident_type": {
    "name": "fraud_incident",
    "display_name": "Fraud Incident",
    "parent_type": "incident_default"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-incident-type-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» incident_type|body|object|true|Details of the incident type to be created.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the Incident Type. Usage of the suffix `_default` is prohibited. This cannot be changed once the incident type has been created.|
|» » display_name|body|string|true|The display name of the Incident Type. Usage of the prefix `PD`, `PagerDuty`, `Default` is prohibited.|
|» » parent_type|body|string|true|The parent type of the Incident Type. Either name or id of the parent type can be used.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether the Incident Type is enabled. Defaults to true if not provided.|
|» » description|body|string|false|The description of the Incident Type.|

## List Incident Type Custom Fields

<a id="opIdlistIncidentTypeCustomFields"></a>

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```

`GET /incidents/types/{type_id_or_name}/custom_fields`

List the custom fields for an incident type.

Custom Fields (CF) are a feature which will allow customers to extend Incidents with their own custom data,
to provide additional context and support features such as customized filtering, search and analytics.
Custom Fields can be applied to different incident types.

Scoped OAuth requires: `custom_fields.read`

## Update a Custom Field for an Incident Type

<a id="opIdupdateIncidentTypeCustomField"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/types/string/custom_fields/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "field": {
      "display_name": "Custom Field 1"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /incidents/types/{type_id_or_name}/custom_fields/{field_id}`

Update a custom field for an incident type. Field Options can also be updated within the same call.

Custom Fields (CF) are a feature which will allow customers to extend Incidents with their own custom data,
to provide additional context and support features such as customized filtering, search and analytics.
Custom Fields can be applied to different incident types.

Scoped OAuth requires: `custom_fields.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "field": {
    "display_name": "Custom Field 1"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-custom-field-for-an-incident-type-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|type_id_or_name|path|string|true|The ID or name of the Incident Type.|
|field_id|path|string|true|The ID of the field.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» field|body|object|true|Details of the custom field to be updated.|
|» » display_name|body|string|false|The display name of the Incident Type.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether the Incident Type is enabled.|
|» » default_value|body|string|false|The default value of the custom field.|
|» » description|body|string|false|The description of the custom field.|
|» » field_options|body|[[CustomFieldsFieldOption](#schemacustomfieldsfieldoption)]|false|List of options to upsert on the custom field. Can only be applied to fields with a `field_type` of `single_value_fixed` or `multi_value_fixed`. When an `id` property is included, this will update the value of the specified field option. Without an `id` property, that field option will be added to the field. Any existing field options not included in the upsert list will be deleted (unless the current default value refers to a field option to be deleted).|

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-incident-workflows">Incident Workflows</h1>

An Incident Workflow is a sequence of configurable Steps and associated Triggers that can execute automated Actions for a given Incident.


## List Incident Workflows

<a id="opIdlistIncidentWorkflows"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incident_workflows \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /incident_workflows`

List existing Incident Workflows.

This is the best method to use to list all Incident Workflows in your account. If your use case requires listing Incident Workflows associated with a particular Service, you can use the "List Triggers" method to find Incident Workflows configured to start for Incidents in a given Service.

An Incident Workflow is a sequence of configurable Steps and associated Triggers that can execute automated Actions for a given Incident.

Scoped OAuth requires: `incident_workflows.read`


<h3 id="list-incident-workflows-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results per page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Offset to start pagination search results.|
|total|query|boolean|false|By default the `total` field in pagination responses is set to `null` to provide the fastest possible response times. Set `total` to `true` for this field to be populated.<br><br>See our [Pagination Docs](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for more information.<br>|
|query|query|string|false|Filters the result, showing only the records whose name matches the query.|
|include[]|query|string|false|Array of additional details to include.|

## List Triggers

<a id="opIdlistIncidentWorkflowTriggers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/incident_workflows/triggers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /incident_workflows/triggers`

List existing Incident Workflow Triggers

Scoped OAuth requires: `incident_workflows.read`


<h3 id="list-triggers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|workflow_id|query|string|false|If provided, only show triggers configured to start the given workflow. Useful for listing all services associated with the given workflow|
|incident_id|query|string|false|If provided, only show triggers configured on the service of the given incident. Useful for finding manual triggers that are configured on the service for a specific incident. Cannot be specified if `service_id` is provided.|
|service_id|query|string|false|If provided, only show triggers configured for incidents in the given service. Useful for listing all workflows associated with the given service. Cannot be specified if `incident_id` is provided.|

## List audit records for an IP allow list

<a id="opIdlistIpAllowListAuditRecords"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/ip_allow_lists/string/audit/records \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /ip_allow_lists/{id}/audit/records`

The response will include audit records with changes that are made to the given IP allow list.

The returned records are sorted by the `execution_time` from newest to oldest.

See [`Cursor-based pagination`](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for instructions on how to paginate through the result set.

For more information see the [Audit API Document](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/audit-records-api/).

Scoped OAuth requires: `audit_records.read`


<h3 id="list-audit-records-for-an-ip-allow-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The minimum of the `limit` parameter used in the request or the maximum request size of the API.|

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-log-entries">Log Entries</h1>

A log of all the events that happen to an Incident, and these are exposed as Log Entries.


## List log entries

<a id="opIdlistLogEntries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/log_entries \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /log_entries`

List all of the incident log entries across the entire account.

A log of all the events that happen to an Incident, and these are exposed as Log Entries.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#log-entries)

Scoped OAuth requires: `incidents.read`


<h3 id="list-log-entries-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results per page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Offset to start pagination search results.|
|total|query|boolean|false|By default the `total` field in pagination responses is set to `null` to provide the fastest possible response times. Set `total` to `true` for this field to be populated.<br><br>See our [Pagination Docs](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for more information.<br>|
|time_zone|query|string(tzinfo)|false|Time zone in which results will be rendered. This will default to the account time zone.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the date range over which you want to search.|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the date range over which you want to search.|
|is_overview|query|boolean|false|If `true`, will return a subset of log entries that show only the most important changes to the incident.|
|include[]|query|string|false|Array of additional Models to include in response.|
|team_ids[]|query|[string]|false|An array of team IDs. Only results related to these teams will be returned. Account must have the `teams` ability to use this parameter.|

|include[]|teams|

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-maintenance-windows">Maintenance Windows</h1>

A Maintenance Window is used to temporarily disable one or more Services for a set period of time.


## List maintenance windows

<a id="opIdlistMaintenanceWindows"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/maintenance_windows \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /maintenance_windows`

List existing maintenance windows, optionally filtered by service and/or team, or whether they are from the past, present or future.

A Maintenance Window is used to temporarily disable one or more Services for a set period of time.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#maintenance-windows)

Scoped OAuth requires: `services.read`
