|query|query|string|false|Filters the result, showing only the records whose name matches the query.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results per page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Offset to start pagination search results.|
|total|query|boolean|false|By default the `total` field in pagination responses is set to `null` to provide the fastest possible response times. Set `total` to `true` for this field to be populated.<br><br>See our [Pagination Docs](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for more information.<br>|
|team_ids[]|query|[string]|false|An array of team IDs. Only results related to these teams will be returned. Account must have the `teams` ability to use this parameter.|
|service_ids[]|query|[string]|false|An array of service IDs. Only results related to these services will be returned.|
|include[]|query|string|false|Array of additional Models to include in response.|
|filter|query|string|false|Only return maintenance windows in a given state.|

`POST /maintenance_windows`

Create a new maintenance window for the specified services. No new incidents will be created for a service that is in maintenance.

A Maintenance Window is used to temporarily disable one or more Services for a set period of time.

```json
    "description": "Immanentizing the eschaton",

        "type": "service_reference"
      }

  }
}
```

## Delete or end a maintenance window

<a id="opIddeleteMaintenanceWindow"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/maintenance_windows/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /maintenance_windows/{id}`

Delete an existing maintenance window if it's in the future, or end it if it's currently on-going. If the maintenance window has already ended it cannot be deleted.

A Maintenance Window is used to temporarily disable one or more Services for a set period of time.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#maintenance-windows)

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-notifications">Notifications</h1>

A Notification is created when an Incident is triggered or escalated.


## List notifications

<a id="opIdlistNotifications"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pagerduty.com/notifications?since=1970-01-01T00%3A00%3A00Z&until=1970-01-01T00%3A00%3A00Z' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /notifications`

List notifications for a given time range, optionally filtered by type (sms_notification, email_notification, phone_notification, or push_notification).

A Notification is created when an Incident is triggered or escalated.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#notifications)

Scoped OAuth requires: `users:notifications.read`


<h3 id="list-notifications-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results per page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Offset to start pagination search results.|
|total|query|boolean|false|By default the `total` field in pagination responses is set to `null` to provide the fastest possible response times. Set `total` to `true` for this field to be populated.<br><br>See our [Pagination Docs](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for more information.<br>|
|time_zone|query|string(tzinfo)|false|Time zone in which results will be rendered. This will default to the account time zone.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|true|The start of the date range over which you want to search. The time element is optional.|
|until|query|string(date-time)|true|The end of the date range over which you want to search. This should be in the same format as since. The size of the date range must be less than 3 months.|
|filter|query|string|false|Return notification of this type only.|
|include[]|query|string|false|Array of additional details to include.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|
|filter|sms_notification|
|filter|email_notification|
|filter|phone_notification|
|filter|push_notification|
|include[]|users|

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-oauth-delegations">OAuth Delegations</h1>

An OAuth Delegation represents a delegation of a User's permissions to an OAuth Client, allowing the client to impersonate the user when making API requests.


## Delete all OAuth delegations

<a id="opIddeleteOauthDelegations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pagerduty.com/oauth_delegations?user_id=string&type=mobile' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /oauth_delegations`

Delete all OAuth delegations as per provided query parameters.

An OAuth delegation represents an instance of a user or account's authorization to an app (via OAuth) to access their PagerDuty account.
Common apps include the PagerDuty mobile app, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and third-party apps. It also represents a user session in the PagerDuty web app.

Deleting an OAuth delegation will revoke that instance of an app's access to that user or account.
To grant access again, reauthorization/reauthentication will be required.

This endpoint supports deleting mobile app OAuth delegations for a given user, which is equivalent to signing users out of the mobile app. It also supports deleting delegations of type web, which is equivalent to signing users out of the web app.

This is a synchronous API.

Scoped OAuth requires: `oauth_delegations.write`


<h3 id="delete-all-oauth-delegations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|user_id|query|string|true|The ID of the user for whom this request is applicable.|
|type|query|string|true|The type of OAuth delegations this request should target. Allowed values are 'mobile' (to sign users out of the mobile app) and 'web' (to sign users out of the web app). You can pass one or more types in, separated by commas (e.g., `type=web,mobile`).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|
|type|mobile|
|type|web|

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-on-calls">On-Calls</h1>

An on-call represents a contiguous unit of time for which a User will be on call for a given Escalation Policy and Escalation Rules


## List all of the on-calls

<a id="opIdlistOnCalls"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/oncalls \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /oncalls`

List the on-call entries during a given time range.

An on-call represents a contiguous unit of time for which a User will be on call for a given Escalation Policy and Escalation Rules.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#on-calls)

Scoped OAuth requires: `oncalls.read`

This API operation has operation specific rate limits. See the [Rate Limits](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/72d3b724589e3-rest-api-rate-limits) page for more information.


<h3 id="list-all-of-the-on-calls-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|time_zone|query|string(tzinfo)|false|Time zone in which results will be rendered. This will default to the account time zone.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results per page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Offset to start pagination search results.|
|total|query|boolean|false|By default the `total` field in pagination responses is set to `null` to provide the fastest possible response times. Set `total` to `true` for this field to be populated.<br><br>See our [Pagination Docs](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for more information.<br>|
|include[]|query|string|false|Array of additional details to include.|
|user_ids[]|query|[string]|false|Filters the results, showing only on-calls for the specified user IDs.|
|escalation_policy_ids[]|query|[string]|false|Filters the results, showing only on-calls for the specified escalation policy IDs.|
|schedule_ids[]|query|[string]|false|Filters the results, showing only on-calls for the specified schedule IDs. If `null` is provided in the array, it includes permanent on-calls due to direct user escalation targets.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the time range over which you want to search. If an on-call period overlaps with the range, it will be included in the result. Defaults to current time. On-call shifts are limited to 90 days in the future.|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the time range over which you want to search. If an on-call period overlaps with the range, it will be included in the result. Defaults to current time. On-call shifts are limited to 90 days in the future, and the `until` time cannot be before the `since` time.|
|earliest|query|boolean|false|This will filter on-calls such that only the earliest on-call for each combination of escalation policy, escalation level, and user is returned. This is useful for determining when the "next" on-calls are for a given set of filters.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|
|include[]|escalation_policies|
|include[]|users|
|include[]|schedules|

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-priorities">Priorities</h1>

A priority is a label representing the importance and impact of an incident. This feature is only available on Standard and Enterprise plans.

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-recommendations">Recommendations</h1>

Recommendations allow you to view and act on AI-generated rule suggestions for your Event Orchestrations. Use these APIs to list recommended rules, accept them into your orchestration, or dismiss them with feedback.


## List recommended rules

<a id="opIdlistRecommendedRules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/recommendations/event_orchestrations/rules \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /recommendations/event_orchestrations/rules`

List AI-generated recommended rules available for an account's Service Event Orchestrations.

Results can be filtered by service or team. Use cursor-based pagination to retrieve large result sets.

Note: `service_id` and `service_ids[]` cannot be used together in the same request.

Scoped OAuth requires: `recommendations.read`


<h3 id="list-recommended-rules-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|service_id|query|string|false|Filter recommended rules for a single service. Cannot be combined with `service_ids[]`.|
|service_ids[]|query|[string]|false|Filter recommended rules for multiple services. Cannot be combined with `service_id`.|
|team_ids[]|query|[string]|false|An array of team IDs. Only results related to these teams will be returned. Account must have the `teams` ability to use this parameter.|
|actions[]|query|[string]|false|Filter recommended rules by action type.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results per page.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Optional parameter used to request the "next" set of results from an API.  The value provided here is most commonly obtained from the `next_cursor` field of the previous request.  When no value is provided, the request starts at the beginning of the result set.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|
|actions[]|suppress|
|actions[]|severity|
|actions[]|priority|

## Dismiss a recommended rule

<a id="opIddismissRecommendedRule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/recommendations/event_orchestrations/services/string/rules/string/dismiss \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "decision": {
      "feedback": "negative"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /recommendations/event_orchestrations/services/{service_id}/rules/{recommendation_id}/dismiss`

Dismiss a recommended rule for a service, recording feedback on whether the recommendation was useful.

Scoped OAuth requires: `recommendations.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "decision": {
    "feedback": "negative"
  }
}
```

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-rulesets">Rulesets</h1>

Rulesets allow you to route events to an endpoint and create collections of Event Rules, which define sets of actions to take based on event content.


## List Rulesets

<a id="opIdlistRulesets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/rulesets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /rulesets`

List all Rulesets
<!-- theme: warning -->
> ### End-of-life
> Rulesets and Event Rules will end-of-life soon. We highly recommend that you [migrate to Event Orchestration](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/migrate-to-event-orchestration) as soon as possible so you can take advantage of the new functionality, such as improved UI, rule creation, APIs and Terraform support, advanced conditions, and rule nesting.

Rulesets allow you to route events to an endpoint and create collections of Event Rules, which define sets of actions to take based on event content.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#rulesets)

Scoped OAuth requires: `event_rules.read`

`DELETE /rulesets/{id}/rules/{rule_id}`

Delete an Event Rule.
<!-- theme: warning -->
> ### End-of-life
> Rulesets and Event Rules will end-of-life soon. We highly recommend that you [migrate to Event Orchestration](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/migrate-to-event-orchestration) as soon as possible so you can take advantage of the new functionality, such as improved UI, rule creation, APIs and Terraform support, advanced conditions, and rule nesting.

Rulesets allow you to route events to an endpoint and create collections of Event Rules, which define sets of actions to take based on event content.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#rulesets)

## List schedules

<a id="opIdlistSchedules"></a>


`GET /schedules`

List the on-call schedules.

A Schedule determines the time periods that users are On-Call.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#schedules)

Scoped OAuth requires: `schedules.read`


<h3 id="list-schedules-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results per page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Offset to start pagination search results.|
|total|query|boolean|false|By default the `total` field in pagination responses is set to `null` to provide the fastest possible response times. Set `total` to `true` for this field to be populated.<br><br>See our [Pagination Docs](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for more information.<br>|
|query|query|string|false|Filters the result, showing only the records whose name matches the query.|
|include[]|query|string|false|Array of additional details to include.|
|time_zone|query|string(tzinfo)|false|Time zone in which results will be rendered. This will default to the current user's time zone and then the account's time zone.|
|include_next_oncall_for_user|query|string|false|Specify an `user_id`, and the schedule list API will return information about this user's next on-call.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the date range over which you want to show schedule entries. Defaults to 2 weeks before until if an until is given. Optional parameter. When provided with include[] for schedule types, populates the rendered_schedule_entries fields in the response.|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the date range over which you want to show schedule entries. Defaults to 2 weeks after since if a since is given. Optional parameter. When provided with include[] for schedule types, populates the rendered_schedule_entries fields in the response.|
|team_ids[]|query|[string]|false|An array of team IDs. Only results related to these teams will be returned. Account must have the `teams` ability to use this parameter.|

## Create a schedule

<a id="opIdcreateSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/schedules \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "schedule": {
      "name": "Daily Engineering Rotation",
      "type": "schedule",
      "time_zone": "America/New_York",
      "description": "Rotation schedule for engineering",
      "schedule_layers": [
        {
          "name": "Night Shift",
          "start": "2015-11-06T20:00:00-05:00",
          "rotation_virtual_start": "2015-11-06T20:00:00-05:00",
          "rotation_turn_length_seconds": 86400,
          "users": [
            {
              "user": {
                "id": "PXPGF42",
                "type": "user_reference"
              }
            }
          ],
          "restrictions": [
            {
              "type": "daily_restriction",
              "start_time_of_day": "08:00:00",
              "duration_seconds": 32400
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /schedules`

Create a new on-call schedule.

A Schedule determines the time periods that users are On-Call.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#schedules)

Scoped OAuth requires: `schedules.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "schedule": {
    "name": "Daily Engineering Rotation",
    "type": "schedule",
    "time_zone": "America/New_York",
    "description": "Rotation schedule for engineering",
    "schedule_layers": [
      {
        "name": "Night Shift",
        "start": "2015-11-06T20:00:00-05:00",
        "rotation_virtual_start": "2015-11-06T20:00:00-05:00",
        "rotation_turn_length_seconds": 86400,
        "users": [
          {
            "user": {
              "id": "PXPGF42",
              "type": "user_reference"
            }
          }
        ],
        "restrictions": [
          {
            "type": "daily_restriction",
            "start_time_of_day": "08:00:00",
            "duration_seconds": 32400
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-schedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|overflow|query|boolean|false|Any on-call schedule entries that pass the date range bounds will be truncated at the bounds, unless the parameter `overflow=true` is passed. This parameter defaults to false.<br>For instance, if your schedule is a rotation that changes daily at midnight UTC, and your date range is from `2011-06-01T10:00:00Z` to `2011-06-01T14:00:00Z`:<br><br><br>- If you don't pass the `overflow=true` parameter, you will get one schedule entry returned with a start of `2011-06-01T10:00:00Z` and end of `2011-06-01T14:00:00Z`.<br>- If you do pass the `overflow=true` parameter, you will get one schedule entry returned with a start of `2011-06-01T00:00:00Z` and end of `2011-06-02T00:00:00Z`.<br>|
|body|body|object|false|The schedule to be created.|
|» schedule|body|[Schedule](#schemaschedule)|true|none|

## Get a schedule

<a id="opIdgetSchedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/schedules/P2LJD7G \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /schedules/{id}`

Show detailed information about a schedule, including entries for each layer.
Scoped OAuth requires: `schedules.read`


<h3 id="get-a-schedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|time_zone|query|string(tzinfo)|false|Time zone in which results will be rendered. This will default to the schedule's time zone.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the date range over which you want to show schedule entries. Defaults to 2 weeks before until if an until is given. Optional parameter. When provided with include[] for schedule types, populates the rendered_schedule_entries fields in the response.|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the date range over which you want to show schedule entries. Defaults to 2 weeks after since if a since is given. Optional parameter. When provided with include[] for schedule types, populates the rendered_schedule_entries fields in the response.|
|overflow|query|boolean|false|Any on-call schedule entries that pass the date range bounds will be truncated at the bounds, unless the parameter `overflow=true` is passed. This parameter defaults to false.<br>For instance, if your schedule is a rotation that changes daily at midnight UTC, and your date range is from `2011-06-01T10:00:00Z` to `2011-06-01T14:00:00Z`:<br><br><br>- If you don't pass the `overflow=true` parameter, you will get one schedule entry returned with a start of `2011-06-01T10:00:00Z` and end of `2011-06-01T14:00:00Z`.<br>- If you do pass the `overflow=true` parameter, you will get one schedule entry returned with a start of `2011-06-01T00:00:00Z` and end of `2011-06-02T00:00:00Z`.<br>|
|include_next_oncall_for_user|query|string|false|Specify an `user_id`, and the schedule list API will return information about this user's next on-call.|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the schedule.|

```json
              "duration_seconds": 32400
            }
```

```bash
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /schedules/{id}`

Update an existing on-call schedule.

A Schedule determines the time periods that users are On-Call.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#schedules)

Scoped OAuth requires: `schedules.write`

## List audit records for a schedule

<a id="opIdlistSchedulesAuditRecords"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/schedules/P2LJD7G/audit/records \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /schedules/{id}/audit/records`

The returned records are sorted by the `execution_time` from newest to oldest.

See [`Cursor-based pagination`](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for instructions on how to paginate through the result set.

For more information see the [Audit API Document](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/audit-records-api/).

Scoped OAuth requires: `audit_records.read`


<h3 id="list-audit-records-for-a-schedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the schedule.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The minimum of the `limit` parameter used in the request or the maximum request size of the API.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Optional parameter used to request the "next" set of results from an API.  The value provided here is most commonly obtained from the `next_cursor` field of the previous request.  When no value is provided, the request starts at the beginning of the result set.<br>|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the date range over which you want to search. If not specified, defaults to `now() - 24 hours` (past 24 hours)|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the date range over which you want to search. If not specified, defaults to `now()`. May not be more than 31 days after `since`.|

## List overrides

<a id="opIdlistScheduleOverrides"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pagerduty.com/schedules/P2LJD7G/overrides?since=2026-04-01T00%3A00%3A00Z&until=2026-05-30T00%3A00%3A00Z' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /schedules/{id}/overrides`

List overrides for a given time range.

A Schedule determines the time periods that users are On-Call.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#schedules)

Scoped OAuth requires: `schedules.read`

|since|query|string(date-time)|true|The start of the date range over which you want to search.|
|until|query|string(date-time)|true|The end of the date range over which you want to search.|
|editable|query|boolean|false|When this parameter is present, only editable overrides will be returned. The result will only include the id of the override if this parameter is present. Only future overrides are editable.|
|overflow|query|boolean|false|Any on-call schedule entries that pass the date range bounds will be truncated at the bounds, unless the parameter overflow=true is passed. This parameter defaults to false.|

## Create one or more overrides

<a id="opIdcreateScheduleOverride"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/schedules/string/overrides \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "overrides": [
      {
        "start": "2012-07-01T00:00:00-04:00",
        "end": "2012-07-02T00:00:00-04:00",
        "user": {
          "id": "PEYSGVA",
          "type": "user_reference"
        },
        "time_zone": "UTC"
      },
      {
        "start": "2012-07-03T00:00:00-04:00",
        "end": "2012-07-04T00:00:00-04:00",
        "user": {
          "id": "PEYSGVF",
          "type": "user_reference"
        },
        "time_zone": "UTC"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /schedules/{id}/overrides`

Create one or more overrides, each for a specific user covering a specified time range. If you create an override on top of an existing override, the last created override will have priority.

A Schedule determines the time periods that users are On-Call.

Note: An older implementation of this endpoint only supported creating a single ocverride per request. That functionality is still supported, but deprecated and may be removed in the future.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#schedules)

Scoped OAuth requires: `schedules.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "overrides": [
    {
      "start": "2012-07-01T00:00:00-04:00",
      "end": "2012-07-02T00:00:00-04:00",
      "user": {
        "id": "PEYSGVA",
        "type": "user_reference"
      },
      "time_zone": "UTC"
    },
    {
      "start": "2012-07-03T00:00:00-04:00",
      "end": "2012-07-04T00:00:00-04:00",
      "user": {
        "id": "PEYSGVF",
        "type": "user_reference"
      },
      "time_zone": "UTC"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Delete an override

<a id="opIddeleteScheduleOverride"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/schedules/string/overrides/Q2MCMG5TVIV6LQ \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /schedules/{id}/overrides/{override_id}`

Remove an override.

You cannot remove a past override.

If the override start time is before the current time, but the end time is after the current time, the override will be truncated to the current time.

If the override is truncated, the status code will be 200 OK, as opposed to a 204 No Content for a successful delete.

A Schedule determines the time periods that users are On-Call.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#schedules)

Scoped OAuth requires: `schedules.write`

|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|
|override_id|path|string|true|The override ID on the schedule.|

## Preview a schedule

<a id="opIdcreateSchedulePreview"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/schedules/preview \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "schedule": {
      "name": "Daily Engineering Rotation",
      "type": "schedule",
      "time_zone": "America/New_York",
      "description": "Rotation schedule for engineering",
      "schedule_layers": [
        {
          "name": "Night Shift",
          "start": "2015-11-06T20:00:00-05:00",
          "end": "2016-11-06T20:00:00-05:00",
          "rotation_virtual_start": "2015-11-06T20:00:00-05:00",
          "rotation_turn_length_seconds": 86400,
          "users": [
            {
              "user": {
                "id": "PXPGF42",
                "type": "user_reference"
              }
            }
          ],
          "restrictions": [
            {
              "type": "daily_restriction",
              "start_time_of_day": "08:00:00",
              "duration_seconds": 32400
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /schedules/preview`

Preview what an on-call schedule would look like without saving it.

A Schedule determines the time periods that users are On-Call.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#schedules)

Scoped OAuth requires: `schedules.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "schedule": {
    "name": "Daily Engineering Rotation",
    "type": "schedule",
    "time_zone": "America/New_York",
    "description": "Rotation schedule for engineering",
    "schedule_layers": [
      {
        "name": "Night Shift",
        "start": "2015-11-06T20:00:00-05:00",
        "end": "2016-11-06T20:00:00-05:00",
        "rotation_virtual_start": "2015-11-06T20:00:00-05:00",
        "rotation_turn_length_seconds": 86400,
        "users": [
          {
            "user": {
              "id": "PXPGF42",
              "type": "user_reference"
            }
          }
        ],
        "restrictions": [
          {
            "type": "daily_restriction",
            "start_time_of_day": "08:00:00",
            "duration_seconds": 32400
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="preview-a-schedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the date range over which you want to search.|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the date range over which you want to search.|
|overflow|query|boolean|false|Any on-call schedule entries that pass the date range bounds will be truncated at the bounds, unless the parameter `overflow=true` is passed. This parameter defaults to false.<br>For instance, if your schedule is a rotation that changes daily at midnight UTC, and your date range is from `2011-06-01T10:00:00Z` to `2011-06-01T14:00:00Z`:<br><br><br>- If you don't pass the `overflow=true` parameter, you will get one schedule entry returned with a start of `2011-06-01T10:00:00Z` and end of `2011-06-01T14:00:00Z`.<br>- If you do pass the `overflow=true` parameter, you will get one schedule entry returned with a start of `2011-06-01T00:00:00Z` and end of `2011-06-02T00:00:00Z`.<br>|
|body|body|object|false|The schedule to be previewed.|
|» schedule|body|[Schedule](#schemaschedule)|true|none|

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-schedulesv3">Schedules_v3</h1>

Shift-Based Schedules API. Creates and manages on-call schedules using a rotation and event model.


<!-- theme: info -->

> **Important note:** Shift-based schedules use the V3 API and are not compatible with V2 automations. **To create automations for Shift-Based Schedules, you need to:**
>
> 1. **Update your automations** to use the V3 API for all new shift-based schedules
> 2. **Keep the V2 endpoint** for your existing schedules
>
> An upgrade tool for existing schedules is coming soon; your legacy schedules will keep working in the meantime. [Learn more](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/shift-based-schedules-api-upgrade-examples).


## List schedules

<a id="opIdlistSchedulesV3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/v3/schedules \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v3/schedules`

<!-- theme: info -->

> **Important note:** Shift-based schedules use the V3 API and are not compatible with V2 automations. **To create automations for Shift-Based Schedules, you need to:**
>
> 1. **Update your automations** to use the V3 API for all new shift-based schedules
> 2. **Keep the V2 endpoint** for your existing schedules
>
> An upgrade tool for existing schedules is coming soon; your legacy schedules will keep working in the meantime. [Learn more](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/shift-based-schedules-api-upgrade-examples).

Retrieve a paginated list of schedule references. Returns lightweight
objects without embedded rotations or events.

Each result is filtered by the caller's read permission; schedules the
caller cannot read are silently excluded.


<h3 id="list-schedules-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Maximum number of schedules to return|
|offset|query|integer|false|none|
|query|query|string|false|Filters the result, showing only the records whose name matches the query.|
|total|query|boolean|false|By default the `total` field in pagination responses is set to `null` to provide the fastest possible response times. Set `total` to `true` for this field to be populated.<br><br>See our [Pagination Docs](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for more information.<br>|
|team_ids[]|query|[string]|false|An array of team IDs. Only results related to these teams will be returned. Account must have the `teams` ability to use this parameter.|
|user_id|query|string|false|Return only schedules that include this user.|

## Create a schedule

<a id="opIdcreateScheduleV3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/v3/schedules \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "schedule": {
      "name": "Engineering On-Call",
```

`POST /v3/schedules`

<!-- theme: info -->

> **Important note:** Shift-based schedules use the V3 API and are not compatible with V2 automations. **To create automations for Shift-Based Schedules, you need to:**
>
> 1. **Update your automations** to use the V3 API for all new shift-based schedules
> 2. **Keep the V2 endpoint** for your existing schedules
>
> An upgrade tool for existing schedules is coming soon; your legacy schedules will keep working in the meantime. [Learn more](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/shift-based-schedules-api-upgrade-examples).

Create a new on-call schedule with basic metadata. Rotations and events
must be added via separate API calls after creation.

**Rejected fields:** `rotations` and `escalation_policies` are not
accepted in the request body and will result in a 400 error.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "schedule": {
    "name": "Engineering On-Call",
    "time_zone": "America/New_York"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-schedule-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateScheduleRequest](#schemacreateschedulerequest)|true|none|

## Get a schedule

<a id="opIdgetScheduleV3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/v3/schedules/PSJUKNI \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v3/schedules/{id}`

<!-- theme: info -->

> **Important note:** Shift-based schedules use the V3 API and are not compatible with V2 automations. **To create automations for Shift-Based Schedules, you need to:**
>
> 1. **Update your automations** to use the V3 API for all new shift-based schedules
> 2. **Keep the V2 endpoint** for your existing schedules
>
> An upgrade tool for existing schedules is coming soon; your legacy schedules will keep working in the meantime. [Learn more](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/shift-based-schedules-api-upgrade-examples).

Retrieve a schedule by ID including rotations and events. Optionally
include the computed final schedule for a time range.

Use `include[]=final_schedule` to get computed on-call assignments.
Use `since` and `until` to specify the time range.


<h3 id="get-a-schedule-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the schedule.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|Start of time range (ISO 8601). Send `since` and `until` together.<br>`since` can be at most 3 years in the future.<br>|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|End of time range (ISO 8601). Send `since` and `until` together.<br>`until` must be after `since`, and can be at most 3 years and 2 weeks<br>in the future.<br>|
|time_zone|query|string|false|IANA timezone identifier for rendering shift times. Defaults to the<br>schedule's configured time zone.<br>|
|overflow|query|boolean|false|Include shifts that extend beyond the requested time range boundaries|
|include[]|query|[string]|false|Additional data to include in the schedule response:<br>- `final_schedule`: computed on-call assignments for the time range<br>- `users`: all users referenced in the schedule<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|include[]|final_schedule|
|include[]|users|

## Update a schedule

<a id="opIdupdateScheduleV3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/v3/schedules/PSJUKNI \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "schedule": {
      "name": "New Schedule Name"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /v3/schedules/{id}`

<!-- theme: info -->

> **Important note:** Shift-based schedules use the V3 API and are not compatible with V2 automations. **To create automations for Shift-Based Schedules, you need to:**
>
> 1. **Update your automations** to use the V3 API for all new shift-based schedules
> 2. **Keep the V2 endpoint** for your existing schedules
>
> An upgrade tool for existing schedules is coming soon; your legacy schedules will keep working in the meantime. [Learn more](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/shift-based-schedules-api-upgrade-examples).

Update schedule metadata (name, description, time zone). `time_zone`
is required; `name` and `description` are optional and keep their
current values when omitted.

To modify rotations or events, use their respective endpoints.

**Rejected fields:** `rotations` and `escalation_policies` are not
accepted and will result in a 400 error.

```json
    "name": "New Schedule Name"
  }
}
```

## List audit records for a schedule

<a id="opIdlistSchedulesAuditRecordsV3"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/v3/schedules/PSJUKNI/audit/records \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v3/schedules/{id}/audit/records`

<!-- theme: info -->

> **Important note:** Shift-based schedules use the V3 API and are not compatible with V2 automations. **To create automations for Shift-Based Schedules, you need to:**
>
> 1. **Update your automations** to use the V3 API for all new shift-based schedules
> 2. **Keep the V2 endpoint** for your existing schedules
>
> An upgrade tool for existing schedules is coming soon; your legacy schedules will keep working in the meantime. [Learn more](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/shift-based-schedules-api-upgrade-examples).

The returned records are sorted by the `execution_time` from newest to oldest.

See [`Cursor-based pagination`](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for instructions on how to paginate through the result set.

For more information see the [Audit API Document](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/audit-records-api/).

Scoped OAuth requires: `audit_records.read`


<h3 id="list-audit-records-for-a-schedule-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the schedule.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The minimum of the `limit` parameter used in the request or the maximum request size of the API.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Optional parameter used to request the "next" set of results from an API.  The value provided here is most commonly obtained from the `next_cursor` field of the previous request.  When no value is provided, the request starts at the beginning of the result set.<br>|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the date range over which you want to search. If not specified, defaults to `now() - 24 hours` (past 24 hours)|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the date range over which you want to search. If not specified, defaults to `now()`. May not be more than 31 days after `since`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|

## List custom shifts

<a id="opIdlistCustomShifts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pagerduty.com/v3/schedules/PSJUKNI/custom_shifts?since=2026-06-01T00%3A00%3A00Z&until=2026-06-28T23%3A59%3A59Z' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v3/schedules/{id}/custom_shifts`

<!-- theme: info -->

> **Important note:** Shift-based schedules use the V3 API and are not compatible with V2 automations. **To create automations for Shift-Based Schedules, you need to:**
>
> 1. **Update your automations** to use the V3 API for all new shift-based schedules
> 2. **Keep the V2 endpoint** for your existing schedules
>
> An upgrade tool for existing schedules is coming soon; your legacy schedules will keep working in the meantime. [Learn more](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/shift-based-schedules-api-upgrade-examples).

Retrieve custom shifts for a schedule within a time range.

**`since` and `until` are required.**

Returns every custom shift that overlaps the window.


<h3 id="list-custom-shifts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the schedule.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|true|Start of time range (ISO 8601). Can be at most 2 years in the future.<br>|
|until|query|string(date-time)|true|End of time range (ISO 8601). Can be at most 2 years and 2 weeks in<br>the future.<br>|
|time_zone|query|string|false|IANA timezone identifier for rendering shift times. Defaults to the<br>schedule's configured time zone.<br>|
|overflow|query|boolean|false|Include shifts that extend beyond the requested time range boundaries|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "custom_shifts": []
}
```

```json
  }
}
```

## Create custom shifts

<a id="opIdcreateCustomShifts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/v3/schedules/PSJUKNI/custom_shifts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "custom_shifts": [
      {
        "type": "custom_shift",
        "start_time": "2025-03-15T09:00:00Z",
        "end_time": "2025-03-15T17:00:00Z",
        "assignments": [
          {
            "type": "shift_assignment",
            "member": {
              "type": "user_member",
              "user_id": "PUSER123"
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v3/schedules/{id}/custom_shifts`

<!-- theme: info -->

> **Important note:** Shift-based schedules use the V3 API and are not compatible with V2 automations. **To create automations for Shift-Based Schedules, you need to:**
>
> 1. **Update your automations** to use the V3 API for all new shift-based schedules
> 2. **Keep the V2 endpoint** for your existing schedules
>
> An upgrade tool for existing schedules is coming soon; your legacy schedules will keep working in the meantime. [Learn more](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/shift-based-schedules-api-upgrade-examples).

Create one or more custom shifts for a schedule. Custom shifts are
ad-hoc one-off coverage periods that exist outside of rotation events.

Each custom shift requires exactly one assignment.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "custom_shifts": [
    {
      "type": "custom_shift",
      "start_time": "2025-03-15T09:00:00Z",
      "end_time": "2025-03-15T17:00:00Z",
      "assignments": [
        {
          "type": "shift_assignment",
          "member": {
            "type": "user_member",
            "user_id": "PUSER123"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## List overrides

<a id="opIdlistOverrides"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pagerduty.com/v3/schedules/PSJUKNI/overrides?since=2026-06-01T00%3A00%3A00Z&until=2026-06-28T23%3A59%3A59Z' \

```

`GET /v3/schedules/{id}/overrides`

<!-- theme: info -->

> **Important note:** Shift-based schedules use the V3 API and are not compatible with V2 automations. **To create automations for Shift-Based Schedules, you need to:**

Retrieve overrides for a schedule within a time range.

**`since` and `until` are required.**

Returns every override that overlaps the window.


<h3 id="list-overrides-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the schedule.|

|until|query|string(date-time)|true|End of time range (ISO 8601). Can be at most 2 years and 2 weeks in<br>the future.<br>|
|time_zone|query|string|false|IANA timezone identifier for rendering shift times. Defaults to the<br>schedule's configured time zone.<br>|
|overflow|query|boolean|false|Include shifts that extend beyond the requested time range boundaries|

## Create overrides

<a id="opIdcreateOverrides"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/v3/schedules/PSJUKNI/overrides \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "overrides": [
      {
        "type": "override_shift",
        "rotation_id": "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXY",
        "start_time": "2025-03-15T09:00:00Z",
        "end_time": "2025-03-15T17:00:00Z",
        "overridden_member": {
          "type": "user_member",
          "user_id": "PUSER123"
        },
        "overriding_member": {
          "type": "user_member",
          "user_id": "PUSER456"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v3/schedules/{id}/overrides`

<!-- theme: info -->

> **Important note:** Shift-based schedules use the V3 API and are not compatible with V2 automations. **To create automations for Shift-Based Schedules, you need to:**
>
> 1. **Update your automations** to use the V3 API for all new shift-based schedules
> 2. **Keep the V2 endpoint** for your existing schedules
>
> An upgrade tool for existing schedules is coming soon; your legacy schedules will keep working in the meantime. [Learn more](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/shift-based-schedules-api-upgrade-examples).

Create one or more overrides for a schedule. An override temporarily
replaces a scheduled on-call member with a different member for a
specific time period.

Each override must reference either a `rotation_id` or a
`custom_shift_id` (not both). The overriding member must belong to
the account.

**Note:** The create response wraps the result in an `overrides` array.
Single-resource endpoints (get, update) wrap in `override` (singular).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "overrides": [
    {
      "type": "override_shift",
      "rotation_id": "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXY",
      "start_time": "2025-03-15T09:00:00Z",
      "end_time": "2025-03-15T17:00:00Z",
      "overridden_member": {
        "type": "user_member",
        "user_id": "PUSER123"
      },
      "overriding_member": {
        "type": "user_member",
        "user_id": "PUSER456"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-overrides-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the schedule.|
|body|body|[CreateOverridesRequest](#schemacreateoverridesrequest)|true|none|
|» overrides|body|[object]|true|none|
|» » type|body|string|false|Optional.|
|» » rotation_id|body|string|false|Mutually exclusive with custom_shift_id|
|» » custom_shift_id|body|string|false|Mutually exclusive with rotation_id|
|» » start_time|body|string(date-time)|true|Must be within one year from now. A value in the past is set<br>to the current time.<br>|
|» » end_time|body|string(date-time)|true|none|
|» » overridden_member|body|[ShiftMember](#schemashiftmember)|true|A member (user) assigned to a shift or rotation slot|
|» » overriding_member|body|[ShiftMember](#schemashiftmember)|true|A member (user) assigned to a shift or rotation slot|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|override_shift|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "overrides": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "type": "override_shift",
      "rotation_id": "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXY2",
      "custom_shift_id": "string",
      "start_time": "2025-03-15T09:00:00Z",
      "end_time": "2025-03-15T17:00:00Z",
      "overridden_member": {
        "type": "user_member",
        "user_id": "PUSER123"
      },
      "overriding_member": {
        "type": "user_member",
        "user_id": "PUSER123"
      },
      "self": "http://example.com",
      "html_url": "http://example.com"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
    "message": "Invalid Request",
    "code": 2001,
    "errors": {
      "event.effective_since": [
        "Date cannot be more than 12 months in the future"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

```json
  "error": {
    "message": "Not Found",
    "code": 2100
  }
}
```

```json
  }
```

<!-- theme: info -->

> **Important note:** Shift-based schedules use the V3 API and are not compatible with V2 automations. **To create automations for Shift-Based Schedules, you need to:**
>

Create a new empty rotation for a schedule. After creating a rotation,
add events to define the on-call pattern.

**Note:** Rotations have no configuration of their own — all scheduling
logic (recurrence, assignment strategy, members) is specified on events.
The request body must be empty or `{}`.


> Body parameter

```json
{}
```

|body|body|object|false|none|

```json
    "id": "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXY2",

    "events": [
      {
        "id": "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXY2",
        "type": "schedule_event",
        "name": "Weekly On-Call",
        "start_time": {
          "date_time": "2025-03-03T09:00:00Z",
          "time_zone": "America/New_York"
        },
        "end_time": {
          "date_time": "2025-03-03T09:00:00Z",
          "time_zone": "America/New_York"
        },
        "effective_since": "2025-03-03T00:00:00Z",
        "effective_until": "2025-09-01T00:00:00Z",
        "recurrence": [
          "RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY"
        ],
        "assignment_strategy": {
          "type": "rotating_member_assignment_strategy",
          "shifts_per_member": 1,
          "members": [
            {
              "type": "user_member",
              "user_id": "PUSER123"
            }
          ]
        },
        "self": "http://example.com",
        "html_url": "http://example.com"
      }
    ],
    "self": "http://example.com",
    "html_url": "http://example.com"
  }
}
```

## Create an event

<a id="opIdcreateEvent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/v3/schedules/PSJUKNI/rotations/AGO462IDT5ZMNFBVSROUDT6B4M/events \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "event": {
      "name": "Weekly On-Call",
      "start_time": {
        "date_time": "2025-03-03T09:00:00Z",
        "time_zone": "America/New_York"
      },
      "end_time": {
        "date_time": "2025-03-10T09:00:00Z",
        "time_zone": "America/New_York"
      },
      "effective_since": "2025-03-03T00:00:00Z",
      "recurrence": [
        "RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY"
      ],
      "assignment_strategy": {
        "type": "rotating_member_assignment_strategy",
        "shifts_per_member": 1,
        "members": [
          {
            "type": "user_member",
            "user_id": "PUSER123"
          },
          {
            "type": "user_member",
            "user_id": "PUSER456"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v3/schedules/{id}/rotations/{rotation_id}/events`

<!-- theme: info -->

> **Important note:** Shift-based schedules use the V3 API and are not compatible with V2 automations. **To create automations for Shift-Based Schedules, you need to:**
>
> 1. **Update your automations** to use the V3 API for all new shift-based schedules
> 2. **Keep the V2 endpoint** for your existing schedules
>
> An upgrade tool for existing schedules is coming soon; your legacy schedules will keep working in the meantime. [Learn more](https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/shift-based-schedules-api-upgrade-examples).

Create a new event that defines when and how users are on-call within
a rotation.

**Constraints:**
- Maximum 5 events per rotation
- Events within a rotation cannot overlap
- `effective_since` must be in the future (past values are clamped to now)
- All users referenced in `assignment_strategy.members` must exist and
  belong to the account


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "event": {
    "name": "Weekly On-Call",
    "start_time": {
      "date_time": "2025-03-03T09:00:00Z",
      "time_zone": "America/New_York"
    },
    "end_time": {
      "date_time": "2025-03-10T09:00:00Z",
      "time_zone": "America/New_York"
    },
    "effective_since": "2025-03-03T00:00:00Z",
    "recurrence": [
      "RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY"
    ],
    "assignment_strategy": {
      "type": "rotating_member_assignment_strategy",
      "shifts_per_member": 1,
      "members": [
        {
          "type": "user_member",
          "user_id": "PUSER123"
        },
        {
          "type": "user_member",
          "user_id": "PUSER456"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-event-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the schedule.|
|rotation_id|path|string|true|The ID of the rotation.|
|body|body|[CreateEventRequest](#schemacreateeventrequest)|true|none|
|» event|body|object|true|none|
|» » name|body|string|true|none|
|» » start_time|body|[ZonedDateTime](#schemazoneddatetime)|true|A time-of-day value with an explicit time zone. Used for event<br>`start_time` and `end_time` to define the recurring window of coverage<br>(e.g., 9 AM–5 PM every Monday in New York).<br>|
|» » end_time|body|[ZonedDateTime](#schemazoneddatetime)|true|A time-of-day value with an explicit time zone. Used for event<br>`start_time` and `end_time` to define the recurring window of coverage<br>(e.g., 9 AM–5 PM every Monday in New York).<br>|
|» » effective_since|body|string(date-time)|true|When this event starts producing shifts. Values in the past are<br>clamped to the current time. Can be at most 12 months in the<br>future.<br>|
|» » effective_until|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|When this event stops producing shifts. Omit or null for indefinite.|
|» » recurrence|body|[string]|true|RFC 5545 recurrence rules. Must be an array containing exactly<br>one RRULE, zero or more EXDATE, and zero or more RDATE.<br><br>The RRULE can repeat at most once per hour.<br><br>**UI editor constraints:** The shift-based schedule editor can<br>only load an event when the RRULE satisfies all of the following:<br>1. A `FREQ` parameter is present.<br>2. `FREQ` is one of `WEEKLY`, `DAILY`, `MONTHLY`, or `HOURLY`.<br>3. All `BYDAY` values are standard two-letter day codes<br>   (`MO`, `TU`, `WE`, `TH`, `FR`, `SA`, `SU`).<br><br>Events that violate any condition display a<br>"can't be edited in the UI" modal and must be managed via the API.<br>|
|» » assignment_strategy|body|[EventAssignmentStrategy](#schemaeventassignmentstrategy)|true|Defines how users are assigned on-call within an event's time window.<br><br>- `rotating_member_assignment_strategy`: users rotate in sequence.<br>  `shifts_per_member` controls how many consecutive shift periods each<br>  member covers before rotating.<br>- `every_member_assignment_strategy`: all listed members are on-call<br>  simultaneously for every occurrence.<br>|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "event": {
    "id": "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXY2",
    "type": "schedule_event",
    "name": "Weekly On-Call",
    "start_time": {
      "date_time": "2025-03-03T09:00:00Z",
      "time_zone": "America/New_York"
    },
    "end_time": {
      "date_time": "2025-03-03T09:00:00Z",
      "time_zone": "America/New_York"
    },
    "effective_since": "2025-03-03T00:00:00Z",
    "effective_until": "2025-09-01T00:00:00Z",
    "recurrence": [
      "RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY"
    ],
    "assignment_strategy": {
      "type": "rotating_member_assignment_strategy",
      "shifts_per_member": 1,
      "members": [
        {
          "type": "user_member",
          "user_id": "PUSER123"
        }
      ]
    },
    "self": "http://example.com",
    "html_url": "http://example.com"
  }
}
```

  be updated

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-service-dependencies">Service Dependencies</h1>

Services are categorized into technical and business services. Dependencies can be created via any combination of these services.


## Associate service dependencies

<a id="opIdcreateServiceDependency"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/service_dependencies/associate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "relationships": [
      {
        "supporting_service": {
          "id": "P7AD56",
          "type": "service"
        },
        "dependent_service": {
          "id": "P99DJ6",
          "type": "business_service"
        }
      },
      {
        "supporting_service": {
          "id": "DT93K1",
          "type": "business_service"
        },
        "dependent_service": {
          "id": "RS34D9",
          "type": "service"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /service_dependencies/associate`

Create new dependencies between two services.

Business services model capabilities that span multiple technical services and that may be owned by several different teams.

A service can have a maximum of 2,000 dependencies with a depth limit of 100. If the limit is reached, the API will respond with an error.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#business-services)

Scoped OAuth requires: `services.write`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "relationships": [
    {
      "supporting_service": {
        "id": "P7AD56",
        "type": "service"
      },
      "dependent_service": {
        "id": "P99DJ6",
        "type": "business_service"
      }
    },

        "id": "DT93K1",

      },
      "dependent_service": {

}
```

## Create a service

<a id="opIdcreateService"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/services \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "service": {
      "type": "service",
      "name": "My Web App",
      "description": "My cool web application that does things.",
      "auto_resolve_timeout": 14400,
      "acknowledgement_timeout": 600,
      "status": "active",
      "escalation_policy": {
        "id": "PWIP6CQ",
        "type": "escalation_policy_reference"
      },
      "incident_urgency_rule": {
        "type": "use_support_hours",
        "during_support_hours": {
          "type": "constant",
          "urgency": "high"
        },
        "outside_support_hours": {
          "type": "constant",
          "urgency": "low"
        }
      },
      "support_hours": {
        "type": "fixed_time_per_day",
        "time_zone": "America/Lima",
        "start_time": "09:00:00",
        "end_time": "17:00:00",
        "days_of_week": [
          1,
          2,
          3,
          4,
          5
        ]
      },
      "scheduled_actions": [
        {
          "type": "urgency_change",
          "at": {
            "type": "named_time",
            "name": "support_hours_start"
          },
          "to_urgency": "high"
        }
      ],
      "alert_creation": "create_alerts_and_incidents",
      "alert_grouping_parameters": {
        "type": "time",
        "config": {
          "timeout": 2
        }
      },
      "auto_pause_notifications_parameters": {
        "enabled": true,
        "timeout": 300
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /services`

Create a new service.

If `status` is included in the request, it must have a value of `active` when creating a new service. If a different status is required, make a second request to update the service.

A service may represent an application, component, or team you wish to open incidents against.

There is a limit of 25,000 services per account. If the limit is reached, the API will respond with an error. There is also a limit of 100,000 open Incidents per Service. If the limit is reached and `auto_resolve_timeout` is disabled (set to 0 or null), the `auto_resolve_timeout` property will automatically be set to  84600 (1 day).

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#services)

Scoped OAuth requires: `services.write`

`PUT /services/{id}`

Update an existing service.

A service may represent an application, component, or team you wish to open incidents against.

There is a limit of 100,000 open Incidents per Service. If the limit is reached and you disable `auto_resolve_timeout` (set to 0 or null), the API will respond with an error.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#services)

Scoped OAuth requires: `services.write`

## Delete a service

<a id="opIddeleteService"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/services/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /services/{id}`

Delete an existing service.

Once the service is deleted, it will not be accessible from the web UI and new incidents won't be able to be created for this service.

A service may represent an application, component, or team you wish to open incidents against.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#services)

## List audit records for a service

<a id="opIdlistServiceAuditRecords"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/services/P2LJD7G/audit/records \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /services/{id}/audit/records`

The returned records are sorted by the `execution_time` from newest to oldest.

See [`Cursor-based pagination`](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for instructions on how to paginate through the result set.

For more information see the [Audit API Document](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/audit-records-api/).

Scoped OAuth requires: `audit_records.read`


<h3 id="list-audit-records-for-a-service-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the schedule.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The minimum of the `limit` parameter used in the request or the maximum request size of the API.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Optional parameter used to request the "next" set of results from an API.  The value provided here is most commonly obtained from the `next_cursor` field of the previous request.  When no value is provided, the request starts at the beginning of the result set.<br>|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the date range over which you want to search. If not specified, defaults to `now() - 24 hours` (past 24 hours)|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the date range over which you want to search. If not specified, defaults to `now()`. May not be more than 31 days after `since`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|

## Convert a Service's Event Rules into Event Orchestration Rules

<a id="opIdconvertServiceEventRulesToEventOrchestration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/services/string/rules/convert \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /services/{id}/rules/convert`

Convert this Service's Event Rules into functionally equivalent Event Orchestration Rules.

Sending a request to this API endpoint has several effects:

1. Automatically creates Event Orchestration Rules for this Service that will behave identically as this Service's currently configured Event Rules.
2. Makes all existing Event Rules for this Service read-only. All future updates need to be made via the newly created Event Orchestration rules.

Sending a request to this API endpoint will **not** change how future events will be processed. If past events for this Service have been evaluated via Event Rules then new events sent to this Service will also continue to be evaluated via the (now read-only) Event Rules. To change this Service so that new events start being evaluated via the newly created Event Orchestration Rules use the [Update the Service Orchestration active status for a Service API](https://developer.pagerduty.com/api-reference/855659be83d9e-update-the-service-orchestration-active-status-for-a-service).

> ### End-of-life
> Event Rules will end-of-life soon. We highly recommend that you use this API to [migrate to Event Orchestration](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/migrate-to-event-orchestration) as soon as possible so you can take advantage of the new functionality, such as improved UI, rule creation, APIs and Terraform support, advanced conditions, and rule nesting.

Scoped OAuth requires: `services.write`

`GET /services/{id}/enablements`

List all feature enablement settings for a service. Currently, only the `aiops` enablement is supported.

For any account with the AIOps product addon, every service will have AIOps features enabled by default.

## Update an Enablement for a Service

<a id="opIdupdateServiceFeatureEnablement"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/services/string/enablements/aiops \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "enablement": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /services/{id}/enablements/{feature_name}`

Update the feature enablement setting for a specific product addon on a service. This setting controls enabling or disabling the set of features contained within the addon.
Currently, only `aiops` is supported as a valid feature enablement.

**Warning conditions**:
- If the account is not entitled to use AIOps features, the setting will be updated, but a warning will be returned.

For PDRP customers, this feature is branded **Signal Intelligence** in the PagerDuty product UI. The API field names and values (e.g. `aiops`) are unchanged.

Scoped OAuth requires: `services.write`

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-sre-agent">SRE Agent</h1>

The SRE Agent uses AI to help manage and resolve incidents. Memories are knowledge learned by the SRE Agent from past incidents and conversations.


## List SRE Agent memories

<a id="opIdlistSreMemories"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/sre_agent/memories \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /sre_agent/memories`

Search SRE Agent memories for the account.

Memories are knowledge learned by the SRE Agent, including service runbooks, service profiles,
incident playbooks, and incident summaries. Filter by service ID, incident ID, or memory type to retrieve
relevant memories.

Scoped OAuth requires: `incident.read`


<h3 id="list-sre-agent-memories-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results to return per page.|
|service_id|query|string|false|Filter memories by service ID|
|incident_id|query|string|false|Filter memories by incident ID|
|type|query|string|false|Filter memories by type|

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-webhooks">Webhooks</h1>

A webhook is a way to receive events that occur on the PagerDuty platform via an HTTP POST request.
V3 webhooks are set up by creating a webhook subscription.


## List webhook subscriptions

<a id="opIdlistWebhookSubscriptions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/webhook_subscriptions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /webhook_subscriptions`

List existing webhook subscriptions.

The `filter_type` and `filter_id` query parameters may be used to only show subscriptions
for a particular _service_ or _team_.

For more information on webhook subscriptions and how they are used to configure v3 webhooks
see the [Webhooks v3 Developer Documentation](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/webhooks/v3-overview/).

Scoped OAuth requires: `webhook_subscriptions.read`


<h3 id="list-webhook-subscriptions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results per page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Offset to start pagination search results.|
|total|query|boolean|false|By default the `total` field in pagination responses is set to `null` to provide the fastest possible response times. Set `total` to `true` for this field to be populated.<br><br>See our [Pagination Docs](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for more information.<br>|
|filter_type|query|string|false|The type of resource to filter upon.|
|filter_id|query|string|false|The id of the resource to filter upon. Required if filter_type is service or team.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|filter_type|account|
|filter_type|service|
|filter_type|team|

> 200 Response

```json
      "delivery_method": {
        "id": "PF9KMXH",
        "secret": null,
        "type": "http_delivery_method",
        "url": "https://example.com/receive_a_pagerduty_webhook",
        "custom_headers": [
          {
            "name": "your-header-name",
            "value": "-- redacted --"
          }
        ]
      },
      "description": "Sends PagerDuty v3 webhook events somewhere interesting.",
      "events": [
        "incident.acknowledged",
        "incident.annotated",
```

## Create a webhook subscription

<a id="opIdcreateWebhookSubscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/webhook_subscriptions \

  -d '{

  }'
```

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-standards">Standards</h1>

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-status-dashboards">Status Dashboards</h1>

## Get impacted Business Services for a Status Dashboard by `id`.

<a id="opIdgetStatusDashboardServiceImpactsById"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/status_dashboards/string/service_impacts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /status_dashboards/{id}/service_impacts`

Get impacted Business Services for a Status Dashboard by `id`

This endpoint does not return an exhaustive list of Business Services but rather provides access to the most impacted on the specified Status Dashboard up to the limit of 200.

The returned Business Services are sorted first by Impact, secondarily by most recently impacted, and finally by name.

To get Impact information about a specific Business Service on the Status Dashboard that does not appear in the Impact-sorted response, use the `ids[]` parameter on the `/business_services/impacts` endpoint.

Scoped OAuth requires: `status_dashboards.read`


<h3 id="get-impacted-business-services-for-a-status-dashboard-by-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|
|additional_fields[]|query|string|false|Provides access to additional fields such as highest priority per business service and total impacted count|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|additional_fields[]|services.highest_impacting_priority|
|additional_fields[]|total_impacted_count|

## Get impacted Business Services for a Status Dashboard by `url_slug`

<a id="opIdgetStatusDashboardServiceImpactsByUrlSlug"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/status_dashboards/url_slugs/string/service_impacts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /status_dashboards/url_slugs/{url_slug}/service_impacts`

Get Business Service Impacts for the Business Services on a Status Dashboard by its `url_slug`. A `url_slug` is a human-readable reference
for a custom Status Dashboard that may be created or changed in the UI. It will generally be a `dash-separated-string-like-this`.

This endpoint does not return an exhaustive list of Business Services but rather provides access to the most impacted on the Status Dashboard up to the limit of 200.

The returned Business Services are sorted first by Impact, secondarily by most recently impacted, and finally by name.

To get impact information about a specific Business Service on the Status Dashboard that does not appear in the Impact-sored response, use the `ids[]` parameter on the `/business_services/impacts` endpoint.

Scoped OAuth requires: `status_dashboards.read`


<h3 id="get-impacted-business-services-for-a-status-dashboard-by-urlslug-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|url_slug|path|string|true|The `url_slug` for a status dashboard|
|additional_fields[]|query|string|false|Provides access to additional fields such as highest priority per business service and total impacted count|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|additional_fields[]|services.highest_impacting_priority|
|additional_fields[]|total_impacted_count|

```json
  ],

    "total_impacted_count": 1
  }
}
```

## Delete a team

<a id="opIddeleteTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/teams/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /teams/{id}`

Remove an existing team.

Succeeds only if the team has no associated Escalation Policies, Services, Schedules and Subteams.

All associated unresovled incidents will be reassigned to another team (if specified) or will loose team association, thus becoming account-level (with visibility implications).

Note that the incidents reassignment process is asynchronous and has no guarantee to complete before the API call return.

A team is a collection of Users and Escalation Policies that represent a group of people within an organization.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#teams)

Scoped OAuth requires: `teams.write`


<h3 id="delete-a-team-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|reassignment_team|query|string|false|Team to reassign unresolved incident to.<br>If an unresolved incident exists on both the reassignment team and<br>the team being deleted, a duplicate will not be made. If not supplied,<br>unresolved incidents will be made account-level.<br>|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|

## List audit records for a team

<a id="opIdlistTeamsAuditRecords"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/teams/string/audit/records \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /teams/{id}/audit/records`

The returned records are sorted by the `execution_time` from newest to oldest.

See [`Cursor-based pagination`](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for instructions on how to paginate through the result set.

For more information see the [Audit API Document](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/audit-records-api/).

Scoped OAuth requires: `audit_records.read`


<h3 id="list-audit-records-for-a-team-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The minimum of the `limit` parameter used in the request or the maximum request size of the API.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Optional parameter used to request the "next" set of results from an API.  The value provided here is most commonly obtained from the `next_cursor` field of the previous request.  When no value is provided, the request starts at the beginning of the result set.<br>|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the date range over which you want to search. If not specified, defaults to `now() - 24 hours` (past 24 hours)|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the date range over which you want to search. If not specified, defaults to `now()`. May not be more than 31 days after `since`.|

## Add a user to a team

<a id="opIdupdateTeamUser"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/teams/string/users/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \

  }'
```

`PUT /teams/{id}/users/{user_id}`

Add a user to a team. Attempting to add a user with the `read_only_user` role will return a 400 error.

A team is a collection of Users and Escalation Policies that represent a group of people within an organization.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#teams)

Scoped OAuth requires: `teams.write`
