<h1 id="pagerduty-api-templates">Templates</h1>

Templates is a new feature which will allow customers to create message templates to be leveraged by (but not limited to) status updates. The API will be secured to customers with the status updates entitlements.


## List templates

<a id="opIdgetTemplates"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/templates \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /templates`

Get a list of all the template on an account

Scoped OAuth requires: `templates.read`


<h3 id="list-templates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results per page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Offset to start pagination search results.|
|total|query|boolean|false|By default the `total` field in pagination responses is set to `null` to provide the fastest possible response times. Set `total` to `true` for this field to be populated.<br><br>See our [Pagination Docs](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for more information.<br>|
|query|query|string|false|Template name or description to search|
|template_type|query|string|false|Filters templates by type.|
|sort_by|query|string|false|Used to specify both the field you wish to sort the results on (name/created_at), as well as the direction (asc/desc) of the results. The sort_by field and direction should be separated by a colon. Sort direction defaults to ascending.|

## Create a template

  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{

      "description": "Sample template description",

        "email_subject": "Sample email Subject",
        "message": "Sample SMS message"
      },
      "name": "Sample Template",
      "template_type": "status_update"
    }
  }'

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-users">Users</h1>

Users are members of a PagerDuty account that have the ability to interact with Incidents and other data on the account.


## List users

<a id="opIdlistUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/users \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /users`

List users of your PagerDuty account, optionally filtered by a search query.

Users are members of a PagerDuty account that have the ability to interact with Incidents and other data on the account.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#users)

Scoped OAuth requires: `users.read`


<h3 id="list-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|query|query|string|false|Filters the result, showing only the records whose name matches the query.|
|team_ids[]|query|[string]|false|An array of team IDs. Only results related to these teams will be returned. Account must have the `teams` ability to use this parameter.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results per page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Offset to start pagination search results.|
|total|query|boolean|false|By default the `total` field in pagination responses is set to `null` to provide the fastest possible response times. Set `total` to `true` for this field to be populated.<br><br>See our [Pagination Docs](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for more information.<br>|
|include[]|query|string|false|Array of additional Models to include in response.|

|Content-Type|application/json|
|include[]|contact_methods|
|include[]|notification_rules|

`POST /users`

Create a new user.

Users are members of a PagerDuty account that have the ability to interact with Incidents and other data on the account.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#users)

## Delete a user

<a id="opIddeleteUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/users/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /users/{id}`

Remove an existing user.

Returns 400 if the user has assigned incidents unless your [pricing plan](https://www.pagerduty.com/pricing) has the `offboarding` feature and the account is [configured](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/offboarding#section-additional-configurations) appropriately.

Note that the incidents reassignment process is asynchronous and has no guarantee to complete before the api call return.

[*Learn more about `offboarding` feature*](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/offboarding).

Users are members of a PagerDuty account that have the ability to interact with Incidents and other data on the account.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#users)

Scoped OAuth requires: `users.write`

## List audit records for a user

<a id="opIdlistUsersAuditRecords"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/users/string/audit/records \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /users/{id}/audit/records`

The response will include audit records with changes that are made to the identified user not changes made by the identified user.


The returned records are sorted by the `execution_time` from newest to oldest.

See [`Cursor-based pagination`](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/pagination/) for instructions on how to paginate through the result set.

For more information see the [Audit API Document](https://developer.pagerduty.com/docs/rest-api-v2/audit-records-api/).

Scoped OAuth requires: `audit_records.read`


<h3 id="list-audit-records-for-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The minimum of the `limit` parameter used in the request or the maximum request size of the API.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Optional parameter used to request the "next" set of results from an API.  The value provided here is most commonly obtained from the `next_cursor` field of the previous request.  When no value is provided, the request starts at the beginning of the result set.<br>|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the date range over which you want to search. If not specified, defaults to `now() - 24 hours` (past 24 hours)|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the date range over which you want to search. If not specified, defaults to `now()`. May not be more than 31 days after `since`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|

## Regenerate a user's calendar feed URL key

<a id="opIdregenerateUserPrivateUrlKey"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/users/string/regenerate_private_url_key \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /users/{id}/regenerate_private_url_key`

Regenerate the private URL key used to construct a user's personal iCal calendar feed URLs
(`http_cal_url` and `web_cal_url`). The old key is immediately invalidated; callers should
update any stored feed subscriptions with the new key.

A user may only regenerate their own key. Account admins may regenerate on behalf of any user.

The calendar feed URLs act as bearer credentials: anyone with the URL can read that user's
on-call calendar without further authentication. Rotate the key here whenever a URL may
have been exposed (for example, if it was shared outside the intended audience or if an
admin with `can_update_user` retrieved it via `GET /users/{id}?include[]=calendar_urls`).

Users are members of a PagerDuty account that have the ability to interact with Incidents and
other data on the account.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#users)

Scoped OAuth requires: `users.write`

|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the resource.|

## Get the current user

<a id="opIdgetCurrentUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/users/me \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /users/me`

Get details about the current user.

This endpoint can only be used with a [user-level API key](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/using-the-api#section-generating-a-personal-rest-api-key) or a key generated through an OAuth flow. This will not work if the request is made with an account-level access token.

Users are members of a PagerDuty account that have the ability to interact with Incidents and other data on the account.

For more information see the [API Concepts Document](../../api-reference/a47605517c19a-api-concepts#users)

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|include[]|query|string|false|Array of additional Models to include in response. Use `calendar_urls` to include `http_cal_url` and `web_cal_url`; account admins with `can_update_user` may use this to retrieve another user's calendar feed URLs. Note that these URLs are bearer credentials: anyone with the URL can read that user's on-call calendar.|

<h1 id="pagerduty-api-workflow-integrations">Workflow Integrations</h1>

Workflow Integrations are a way to connect PagerDuty to other tools and services.


## List Workflow Integrations

<a id="opIdlistWorkflowIntegrations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/workflows/integrations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /workflows/integrations`

List available Workflow Integrations.

Scoped OAuth requires: `workflow_integrations.read`


<h3 id="list-workflow-integrations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|limit|query|integer|false|The minimum of the `limit` parameter used in the request or the maximum request size of the API.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Optional parameter used to request the "next" set of results from an API.  The value provided here is most commonly obtained from the `next_cursor` field of the previous request.  When no value is provided, the request starts at the beginning of the result set.<br>|
|include_deprecated|query|boolean|false|Whether to include deprecated Integrations in the response.|

## Get an account's session configurations

<a id="opIdgetSessionConfigurations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.pagerduty.com/session_configurations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /session_configurations`

Retrieves session configurations for a PagerDuty account. Returns an array containing
the requested configurations. If a specific type is requested, the array contains one item.
If no type is specified, the array contains all available configurations (mobile and web).
If no configurations exist, a 404 Not Found error will be returned.

A Session Configuration needs to be created before it can be retrieved and used.

Scoped OAuth requires: `session_configurations.read`


<h3 id="get-an-accounts-session-configurations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|type|query|string|false|Session configuration type. If omitted, returns both mobile and web configurations.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|
|type|mobile|
|type|web|

      "idle_session_ttl": 1200
    }
  ]
}

## Configure an account's session configurations

<a id="opIdupdateSessionConfigurations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pagerduty.com/session_configurations?type=mobile' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "session_configuration": {
      "absolute_session_ttl": 3600,
      "idle_session_ttl": 600
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /session_configurations`

Creates or updates session configurations for a PagerDuty Account. The configurations will take effect immediately for new sessions, while existing sessions for the specified `types` are immediately revoked.

Scoped OAuth requires: `session_configurations.write`

## Delete an account's session configurations.

<a id="opIddeleteSessionConfigurations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.pagerduty.com/session_configurations?type=mobile' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /session_configurations`

Deletes the session configurations for a PagerDuty account that was previously set.
The type parameter is required and specifies which configurations to delete.
A single type ('mobile' or 'web') or comma-separated list may be passed in.

Scoped OAuth requires: `session_configurations.write`


<h3 id="delete-an-accounts-session-configurations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Accept|header|string|true|The `Accept` header is used as a versioning header.|
|Content-Type|header|string|true|none|
|type|query|string|true|Session configuration type. This can be either 'mobile' or 'web', or a comma-separated list of both.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|
|type|mobile|
|type|web|

<h2 id="tocS_ServiceNowFieldMapping">ServiceNowFieldMapping</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaservicenowfieldmapping"></a>
<a id="schema_ServiceNowFieldMapping"></a>
<a id="tocSservicenowfieldmapping"></a>
<a id="tocsservicenowfieldmapping"></a>

```json
{
  "servicenow_field": "string",
  "event_field": "string",
  "type": "query"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|servicenow_field|string|true|none|The ServiceNow field (column) to read the value from. Dot-walked fields are supported to traverse relationships (for example, `support_group.manager.email`).|
|event_field|string|true|none|The event field that the ServiceNow value is mapped to.|
|type|string|false|none|Determines how the field is used during enrichment. `enriched` fields add contextual data to a matched event, while `query` fields are used to match incoming events to Configuration Items. When no mapping specifies a `type`, the field defaults to `enriched` and the `name` field is automatically used as the single query field. To match on a different field — or on more than one field — set `type: query` on those mappings; in that mode `name` is no longer used as a query field unless it is itself marked `query`. Up to 3 query fields may be configured, and when more than one is set an event must contain a matching value for every query field to be enriched (logical AND). At least one mapping must be an enriched field. In responses, a mapping's `type` is `query`, `enriched`, or `discriminator`. `discriminator` is assigned automatically to the `sys_id` field of `cmdb_rel_ci` relationship tables to distinguish relationship types; it appears in responses but cannot be set on requests.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|query|
|type|enriched|
|type|discriminator|

|priority_name|string \| null|false|none|The user-provided short name of the priority.|
|priority_order|integer \| null|false|none|The numerical value used to sort priorities. Higher values are higher priority.|
|reassignment_count|integer|false|none|Total count of reassignments in the incident.|
|resolved_at|string|false|none|Timestamp of when the incident was resolved.|
|resolved_by_user_id|string|false|none|ID of the user who resolved the incident.|
|resolved_by_user_name|string|false|none|Name of the user who resolved the incident.|
|seconds_to_engage|integer|false|none|A measure of *people response time*. This metric measures the time from<br>the first user engagement (acknowledge or responder accept) to the last.<br>This metric is only used for incidents with **multiple responders**;<br>for incidents with one or no engaged users, this value is null.|
|seconds_to_first_ack|integer|false|none|Time between the start of an incident, and the first responder to acknowledge.|
|seconds_to_mobilize|integer|false|none|Time between the start of an incident, and the last additional responder to acknowledge. If an incident has one or no responders, the value will be null.|
|seconds_to_resolve|integer|false|none|Time from when an incident was triggered until it was resolved.|
|service_id|string|false|none|ID of the service that the incident triggered on.|
|service_name|string|false|none|Name of the service that the incident triggered on.|
|sleep_hour_interruptions|integer|false|none|Total number of unique interruptions during sleep hours; 10pm-8am every day, based on the user’s time zone.|
|snoozed_seconds|integer|false|none|Total seconds the incident has been snoozed for.|
|status|string|false|none|The incident status. Can be one of `triggered`, `acknowledged`, or `resolved`.|
|team_id|string \| null|false|none|ID of the team the incident was assigned to.|
|team_name|string \| null|false|none|Name of the team the incident was assigned to.|
|timeout_escalation_count|integer|false|none|Total count of timeout escalations in the incident.|
|total_interruptions|integer|false|none|Total number of unique interruptions in the incident.|
|total_notifications|integer|false|none|Total number of notifications sent for the incident.|
|urgency|string|false|none|Notification level|
|user_defined_effort_seconds|integer \| null|false|none|The total response effort in seconds,<br>[as defined by the user](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/editing-incidents#edit-incident-duration).|

{
  "aggregate": "all, any",
  "fields": [
    "string"
  ],
  "time_window": 300,
  "recommended_time_window": 0
}
```

The configuration for Content Based Intelligent Alert Grouping

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregate|string|false|none|Whether Alerts should be grouped if `all` or `any` specified fields match. If `all` is selected, an exact match on every specified field name must occur for Alerts to be grouped. If `any` is selected, Alerts will be grouped when there is an exact match on at least one of the specified fields.|
|fields|[string]|false|none|An array of strings which represent the fields with which to group against. Depending on the aggregate, Alerts will group if some or all the fields match.|
|time_window|integer|false|none|The maximum amount of time allowed between Alerts. Any Alerts arriving greater than `time_window` seconds apart will not be grouped together. This is a rolling time window up to 24 hours and is counted from the most recently grouped alert. The window is extended every time a new alert is added to the group, up to 24 hours (24 hours only applies to single-service settings). To use the "recommended_time_window," set the value to 0, otherwise the value must be between 300 <= time_window <= 3600.|
|recommended_time_window|integer|false|read-only|In order to ensure your Service has the optimal grouping window, we use data science to calculate your Service's average Alert inter-arrival time. We encourage customers to use this value. Please set `time_window` to 0 to use the `recommended_time_window`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|aggregate|all, any|

The configuration for Intelligent Alert Grouping. Note that this configuration is only available for certain plans.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|time_window|integer|false|none|The maximum amount of time allowed between Alerts. Any Alerts arriving greater than `time_window` seconds apart will not be grouped together. This is a rolling time window and is counted from the most recently grouped alert. The window is extended every time a new alert is added to the group, up to 24 hours. To use the "recommended_time_window," set the value to 0, otherwise the value must be between 300 and 3600.|
|recommended_time_window|integer|false|read-only|In order to ensure your Service has the optimal grouping window, we use data science to calculate your Service's average Alert inter-arrival time. We encourage customers to use this value. Please set `time_window` to 0 to use the `recommended_time_window`.|

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "summary": "string",
  "host": "string",
  "service": "string",
  "state": "string",
  "details": {},
  "user": {},
  "team": {},
  "notification": {
    "id": "string",
    "type": "sms_notification",
    "started_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "address": "string",
    "user": {
      "id": "string",
      "summary": "string",
      "type": "user_reference",
      "self": "http://example.com",
      "html_url": "http://example.com"
    },
    "conferenceAddress": "string",
    "status": "string",
    "": "string"
  },
  "channel": {},
  "changeset": {
    "customer_fields": [
      {
        "id": "PDB5RLI",
        "name": "serial_number_hardware",
        "value": 0,
        "namespace": "incidents",
        "old_value": null
      }
    ],
    "application_fields": [
      {
        "id": "PIJ90N7",
        "name": "service",
        "value": "PIZW265",
        "namespace": "incidents",
        "old_value": null
      }
    ],
    "custom_attributes": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "customer_schema": {
      "old_value": null
    }
  }
}
```

Polymorphic object representation of the means by which the action was channeled. Has different formats depending on type, indicated by channel[type]. Will be one of `auto`, `email`, `api`, `nagios`, or `timeout` if `agent[type]` is `service`. Will be one of `email`, `sms`, `website`, `web_trigger`, or `note` if `agent[type]` is `user`.

An Incident Review is a structured, post-resolution record of what happened during an Incident. Each Incident has at most one Incident Review.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|read-only|The unique identifier of the Incident Review.|
|incident_id|string|false|read-only|The ID of the Incident this Incident Review describes.|
|title|string|false|none|The title of the Incident Review.|
|status|string|false|none|The status of the Incident Review.<br><br>Moving to `completed` is rejected while any required section is still unfilled.<br><br>On accounts where completed Incident Reviews are read-only, a `completed` Incident Review cannot be changed until it is reopened by setting another status.<br>|
|sections|[[IncidentReviewSection](#schemaincidentreviewsection)]|false|read-only|The sections of the Incident Review, ordered by `priority`.|
|generation_status|string|false|read-only|Whether an AI draft is currently being generated for this Incident Review. While this is `generating`, section content is still being written and the Incident Review should be re-fetched to see the result.<br>|
|ai_generated|boolean|false|read-only|Whether this Incident Review has been through the AI draft flow.|
|template_id|string \| null|false|read-only|The ID of the template this Incident Review currently follows, or `null` if it does not follow one.|
|has_events|boolean|false|read-only|Whether the Incident Review has at least one event on its timeline.|
|action_item_count|integer|false|read-only|The total number of action items on this Incident Review.|
|completed_action_item_count|integer|false|read-only|The number of completed action items on this Incident Review.|
|created_by|string \| null|false|read-only|The ID of the User who created this Incident Review, or `null` if it was not created by a User.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The time the Incident Review was created.|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The time the Incident Review was last modified.|
|completed_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|The time the Incident Review was completed, or `null` if it has not been completed.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|status|in_review|
|status|completed|
|generation_status|idle|
|generation_status|generating|

A single CIDR entry within an IP allow list.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cidr|string|true|none|An IPv4 CIDR range. Each octet must be `0`-`255` and the mask must be between `1` and `32`.|

<h2 id="tocS_IpAllowList">IpAllowList</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaipallowlist"></a>
<a id="schema_IpAllowList"></a>
<a id="tocSipallowlist"></a>
<a id="tocsipallowlist"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "AGIS47HYOV6BDODBTMQKMPQPHU",
  "type": "ip_allow_list",
  "state": "enabled",
  "cidr_entries": [
    {
      "cidr": "192.168.1.0/24",
      "description": "Office VPN"
    },
    {
      "cidr": "10.0.0.0/24",
      "description": "Data Center"
    }
  ]
}
```

An IP allow list restricts access to a PagerDuty account's subdomain to a set
of IPv4 CIDR ranges. Enforcement currently applies to web and mobile
application traffic.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|read-only|Unique identifier for the allow list<br>(e.g. `AGIS47HYOV6BDODBTMQKMPQPHU`).<br>|
|type|string|false|read-only|A string that determines the schema of the object.|
|state|string|true|none|Whether the allow list is enforced for the account. When `enabled`, only<br>requests from IPs matching one of the `cidr_entries` are permitted to<br>access the subdomain. When `disabled`, the allow list is stored but not<br>enforced.<br>|
|cidr_entries|[[CidrEntry](#schemacidrentry)]|true|none|The CIDR ranges that are allowed when the allow list is `enabled`. Must<br>be non-empty when `state` is `enabled`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|ip_allow_list|
|state|enabled|
|state|disabled|

|type|string|false|none|The type of action being reported by this message. * `incident.trigger` - Sent when an incident is newly created/triggered. * `incident.acknowledge` - Sent when an incident is acknowledged by a user. * `incident.unacknowledge` - Sent when an incident is unacknowledged due to its acknowledgement timing out. * `incident.resolve` - Sent when an incident has been resolved. * `incident.assign` - Sent when an incident has been assigned to another user. Often occurs in concert with an `acknowledge`. * `incident.escalate` - Sent when an incident has been escalated to another user in the same escalation chain. * `incident.delegate` - Sent when an incident has been reassigned to another escalation policy. * `incident.annotate` - Sent when a note is created on an incident.<br>|
|incident|[Incident](#schemaincident)|false|none|none|
|log_entries|[[AcknowledgeLogEntry](#schemaacknowledgelogentry) \| [AnnotateLogEntry](#schemaannotatelogentry) \| [AssignLogEntry](#schemaassignlogentry) \| [DelegateLogEntry](#schemadelegatelogentry) \| [EscalateLogEntry](#schemaescalatelogentry) \| [ExhaustEscalationPathLogEntry](#schemaexhaustescalationpathlogentry) \| [NotifyLogEntry](#schemanotifylogentry) \| [ReachAckLimitLogEntry](#schemareachacklimitlogentry) \| [ReachTriggerLimitLogEntry](#schemareachtriggerlimitlogentry) \| [RepeatEscalationPathLogEntry](#schemarepeatescalationpathlogentry) \| [ResolveLogEntry](#schemaresolvelogentry) \| [SnoozeLogEntry](#schemasnoozelogentry) \| [TriggerLogEntry](#schematriggerlogentry) \| [UnacknowledgeLogEntry](#schemaunacknowledgelogentry) \| [UrgencyChangeLogEntry](#schemaurgencychangelogentry)]|false|none|Log Entries that correspond to the action this Webhook is reporting. Includes the channels.|

<h2 id="tocS_ContentBasedAlertGroupingConfiguration">ContentBasedAlertGroupingConfiguration</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacontentbasedalertgroupingconfiguration"></a>
<a id="schema_ContentBasedAlertGroupingConfiguration"></a>
<a id="tocScontentbasedalertgroupingconfiguration"></a>
<a id="tocscontentbasedalertgroupingconfiguration"></a>

```json
{
  "aggregate": "all, any",
  "fields": [
    "string"
  ],
  "time_window": 300,
  "recommended_time_window": 0
}
```

The configuration for Content Based Alert Grouping

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregate|string|false|none|Whether Alerts should be grouped if `all` or `any` specified fields match. If `all` is selected, an exact match on every specified field name must occur for Alerts to be grouped. If `any` is selected, Alerts will be grouped when there is an exact match on at least one of the specified fields.|
|fields|[string]|false|none|An array of strings which represent the fields with which to group against. Depending on the aggregate, Alerts will group if some or all the fields match.|
|time_window|integer|false|none|The maximum amount of time allowed between Alerts. Any Alerts arriving greater than `time_window` seconds apart will not be grouped together. This is a rolling time window up to 24 hours and is counted from the most recently grouped alert. The window is extended every time a new alert is added to the group, up to 24 hours (24 hours only applies to single-service settings). To use the "recommended_time_window," set the value to 0, otherwise the value must be between 300 <= time_window <= 3600 or 86400(i.e. 24 hours).|
|recommended_time_window|integer|false|read-only|In order to ensure your Service has the optimal grouping window, we use data science to calculate your Service's average Alert inter-arrival time. We encourage customers to use this value. Please set `time_window` to 0 to use the `recommended_time_window`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|aggregate|all, any|

      "type": "business_service_reference",
      "self": "http://example.com"
    }
  ],
  "supporting_services": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "type": "business_service_reference",
      "self": "http://example.com"
    }
  ]
}
```

The data for a type of relationship where the Incident is related due to Business or Technical Service dependencies.

Both `dependent_services` and `supporting_services` are returned to signify the dependencies between the Services
that the Incident and Related Incident belong to.

Each Service reference returned in the list of supporting and dependent Services has a type of:
[business_service_reference, technical_service_reference].

{
  "orchestration_path": {

      "id": "PC2D9ML",

    },

    "sets": [
      {
        "id": "start",
        "rules": [
          {
            "label": "Always apply some consistent event transformations to all events",
            "id": "c91f72f3",
            "conditions": [],
            "actions": {
              "variables": [
                {
                  "name": "hostname",
                  "path": "event.component",
                  "value": "hostname: (.*)",
                  "type": "regex"
                }
              ],
              "extractions": [
                {
                  "template": "{{variables.hostname}}",
                  "target": "event.custom_details.hostname"
                },
                {
                  "source": "event.source",
                  "regex": "www (.*) service",
                  "target": "event.source"
                }
              ],
              "incident_custom_field_updates": [
                {
                  "id": "PEXCK89",
                  "value": "#my-team-channel"
                },
                {
                  "id": "PN1C4A2",
                  "value": "{{event.timestamp}}"
                }
              ],
              "route_to": "step-two"
            }
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "id": "step-two",
        "rules": [
          {
            "label": "All critical alerts should be treated as P1 incidents",
            "id": "7c54529d",
            "conditions": [
              "event.severity matches 'critical'"
            ],
            "actions": {
              "annotate": "Please use our P1 runbook: https://docs.test/p1-runbook",
              "priority": "P0IN2KQ",
              "suppress": false,
              "incident_custom_field_updates": [
                {
                  "id": "PEXCK89",
                  "value": "#p1-incident-response"
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "label": "If the API endpoints return HTTP 502 run an Automation Action that restarts the service",
            "id": "8a874630",
            "conditions": [
              "event.custom_details.http_status_code equals '502'"
            ],
            "actions": {
              "pagerduty_automation_actions": [
                {
                  "action_id": "01CSB5SMOKCKVRI5GN0LJG7SMB",
                  "trigger_types": [
                    "alert_triggered"
                  ]
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "label": "If there's something wrong on the canary let the team know about it in our deployments Slack channel",
            "id": "1f6d9a33",
            "conditions": [
              "event.custom_details.hostname matches part 'canary'"
            ],
            "actions": {
              "automation_actions": [
                {
                  "name": "Canary Slack Notification",
                  "url": "https://our-slack-listerner.test/send-notification",
                  "auto_send": true,
                  "headers": [
                    {
                      "key": "X-Notification-Source",
                      "value": "PagerDuty Incident Webhook"
                    }
                  ],
                  "parameters": [
                    {
                      "key": "channel",
                      "value": "#my-team-channel"
                    },
                    {
                      "key": "message",
                      "value": "Something is wrong with the canary deployment"
                    }
                  ],
                  "trigger_types": [
                    "alert_triggered"
                  ]
                }
              ],
              "incident_custom_field_updates": [
                {
                  "id": "PEXCK89",
                  "value": "#my-team-channel"
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "label": "Pause the alert and trigger a reboot action if flaky server receives an error",
            "id": "c0163dbe",
            "conditions": [
              {
                "expression": "event.custom_details.hostname matches part 'staging'"
              }
            ],
            "actions": {
              "suspend": 300,
              "pagerduty_automation_actions": [
                {
                  "action_id": "01CSBCGJXMG7ABIJZKPD8P9RCL",
                  "trigger_types": [
                    "alert_suspended"
                  ]
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "label": "Never bother the on-call for info-level events outside of work hours",
            "id": "cd770384",
            "conditions": [
              "event.severity matches 'info' and not (now in Mon,Tue,Wed,Thu,Fri 09:00:00 to 17:00:00 America/Los_Angeles)"
            ],
            "actions": {
              "suppress": true
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "catch_all": {
      "actions": {
        "suppress": true,

          }
        ]

The API field names and values (e.g. `aiops_routing_mismatch`,<br>`aiops_routing`) are unchanged.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_EventAssignmentStrategy">EventAssignmentStrategy</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaeventassignmentstrategy"></a>
<a id="schema_EventAssignmentStrategy"></a>
<a id="tocSeventassignmentstrategy"></a>
<a id="tocseventassignmentstrategy"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "rotating_member_assignment_strategy",
  "shifts_per_member": 1,
  "members": [
    {
      "type": "user_member",
      "user_id": "PUSER123"
    }
  ]
}
```

Defines how users are assigned on-call within an event's time window.

- `rotating_member_assignment_strategy`: users rotate in sequence.
  `shifts_per_member` controls how many consecutive shift periods each
  member covers before rotating.
- `every_member_assignment_strategy`: all listed members are on-call
  simultaneously for every occurrence.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|shifts_per_member|integer|false|none|Required for `rotating_member_assignment_strategy`. Number of<br>consecutive shift occurrences each member covers before the<br>next member takes over.<br><br>Must be omitted (or null) for `every_member_assignment_strategy`.<br><br>**UI editor constraint:** When `recurrence` uses `FREQ=WEEKLY`,<br>`shifts_per_member` must be evenly divisible by the number of days<br>listed in the RRULE `BYDAY` parameter. Events that violate this<br>are fully functional via the API but cannot be loaded in the<br>web schedule editor.<br>|
|members|[[ShiftMember](#schemashiftmember)]|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|rotating_member_assignment_strategy|
|type|every_member_assignment_strategy|

<h2 id="tocS_Event">Event</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaevent"></a>
<a id="schema_Event"></a>
<a id="tocSevent"></a>
<a id="tocsevent"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXY2",
  "type": "schedule_event",
  "name": "Weekly On-Call",
  "start_time": {
    "date_time": "2025-03-03T09:00:00Z",
    "time_zone": "America/New_York"
  },
  "end_time": {
    "date_time": "2025-03-03T09:00:00Z",
    "time_zone": "America/New_York"
  },
  "effective_since": "2025-03-03T00:00:00Z",
  "effective_until": "2025-09-01T00:00:00Z",
  "recurrence": [
    "RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY"
  ],
  "assignment_strategy": {
    "type": "rotating_member_assignment_strategy",
    "shifts_per_member": 1,
    "members": [
      {
        "type": "user_member",
        "user_id": "PUSER123"
      }
    ]
  },
  "self": "http://example.com",
  "html_url": "http://example.com"
}
```

An event defines when and how users are on-call within a rotation.
It combines a recurring time window (`start_time`, `end_time`,
`recurrence`) with an assignment strategy and an effective date range
(`effective_since`, `effective_until`).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|none|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|name|string|true|none|Display name for this event|
|start_time|[ZonedDateTime](#schemazoneddatetime)|true|none|A time-of-day value with an explicit time zone. Used for event<br>`start_time` and `end_time` to define the recurring window of coverage<br>(e.g., 9 AM–5 PM every Monday in New York).<br>|
|end_time|[ZonedDateTime](#schemazoneddatetime)|true|none|A time-of-day value with an explicit time zone. Used for event<br>`start_time` and `end_time` to define the recurring window of coverage<br>(e.g., 9 AM–5 PM every Monday in New York).<br>|
|effective_since|string(date-time)|true|none|When this event starts producing shifts (UTC)|
|effective_until|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When this event stops producing shifts (UTC). Null means indefinite.|
|recurrence|[string]|true|none|RFC 5545 recurrence rules defining the repeating pattern. This must be an array containing:  <br> - Exactly one <b>RRULE</b> <br>- Zero or more <b>EXDATE</b> <br>- Zero or more <b>RDATE</b>|
|assignment_strategy|[EventAssignmentStrategy](#schemaeventassignmentstrategy)|true|none|Defines how users are assigned on-call within an event's time window.<br><br>- `rotating_member_assignment_strategy`: users rotate in sequence.<br>  `shifts_per_member` controls how many consecutive shift periods each<br>  member covers before rotating.<br>- `every_member_assignment_strategy`: all listed members are on-call<br>  simultaneously for every occurrence.<br>|
|self|string(uri)|false|none|none|
|html_url|string(uri)|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|schedule_event|

<h2 id="tocS_UpdateEventRequest">UpdateEventRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaupdateeventrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_UpdateEventRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSupdateeventrequest"></a>
<a id="tocsupdateeventrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "event": {
    "name": "string",
    "start_time": {
      "date_time": "2025-03-03T09:00:00Z",
      "time_zone": "America/New_York"
    },
    "end_time": {
      "date_time": "2025-03-03T09:00:00Z",
      "time_zone": "America/New_York"
    },
    "effective_since": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "effective_until": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "recurrence": [
      "string"
    ],
    "assignment_strategy": {
      "type": "rotating_member_assignment_strategy",
      "shifts_per_member": 1,
      "members": [
        {
          "type": "user_member",
          "user_id": "PUSER123"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

The request replaces the full event. Send every required field,
even the fields that do not change. Get the current values with
`GET /v3/schedules/{id}/rotations/{rotation_id}/events/{event_id}`.

Which fields can be changed depends on the
event's current state:
- Active events (already started): only `effective_until` can be changed
- Future events: all fields can be changed
- Past events: no fields can be changed (returns 400)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event|object|true|none|none|
